definition_zh: 间接的；迂回的；不直截了当的
definition_en: not going straight from one point to another, or not stated openly
core_image: 一条绕过小山的路，虽远却通向同一座村庄
scene: 想问别人的年龄，直接问不太礼貌，只好绕着说。 The flight is indirect and takes two days.
sceneCN: 这里 indirect 是「不直飞的」（第 1 个义项：路线不直）；句意是这趟航班要中转，走两天。

pos.zh: 形容词：间接的；迂回的；不直截了当的

derivatives.zh: 义为「间接地」，由本词加 -ly 构成
义为「直接的」，去掉 in- 即成肯定形式

senses.title: Not straight in route
senses.definition: not going straight, but by a longer way
senses.definitionCN: 不取直路，而是绕更远的路
senses.example: The flight is indirect and takes two days.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟航班要中转，走两天。
senses.why: The Latin regere means to rule or guide straight, and in- removes the straightness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regere 意为「指引成直线」，in- 则取消了这份笔直。

senses.title: Not said or done openly
senses.titleCN: 不直说：含蓄或迂回的表达
senses.definition: not expressed in plain words, so that a listener must infer it
senses.definitionCN: 不用直白的话表达，听者须自行体会
senses.example: She made an indirect suggestion about leaving early.
senses.exampleCN: 她含蓄地提了一句早点走。
senses.why: A bend in the road becomes a bend in speech, used when plainness would be rude.
senses.whyCN: 道路的弯折变成话语的弯折，在直说会失礼时使用。

senses.title: As a secondary effect
senses.definition: happening as a result of something else rather than immediately
senses.definitionCN: 作为他事的结果而发生，而非直接产生
senses.example: The new road had indirect effects on local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新路对本地商店产生了间接影响。
senses.why: Causes can work through a middle object, and the word marks that missing link.
senses.whyCN: 原因可以经由一个中间环节起作用，这个词就标出这条隐藏的链。

senses.title: Of light or cost, reflected
senses.titleCN: 间接的：光线或费用经反射、转嫁
senses.definition: of light, coming from a surface rather than the source; of costs, paid other than by direct charges
senses.definitionCN: 光线经表面反射而来；费用不经直接收取而是转嫁
senses.example: Soft indirect lighting makes the room feel bigger.
senses.exampleCN: 柔和的间接照明让房间显得更大。
senses.why: The same bend applies to physics and to money: the light and the cost both arrive by a detour.
senses.whyCN: 同一道弯折也适用于物理与金钱：光和钱都是绕道而来的。

senses.title: In grammar, reported speech
senses.titleCN: 间接引语：语法上的转述
senses.definition: used in grammar of speech reported without quotation marks
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指不用引号转述他人话语
senses.example: Change the sentence into indirect speech.
senses.exampleCN: 把这句话改成间接引语。
senses.why: Reported speech is one step away from the original voice, another detour.
senses.whyCN: 转述离原声已隔了一层，又是一次绕道。

intro.en: Indirect is in-, not, plus direct, from Latin dirigere, to set straight.
intro.cn: indirect 是 in-（不）加 direct，后者源自拉丁语 dirigere「使之笔直」。

items.en: Dirigere meant to set in line or to guide.
items.cn: dirigere 意为排成直线或引导。

items.en: Indirectus meant winding, not straight.
items.cn: indirectus 意为弯曲的、不直的。

items.en: English used indirect for crooked paths and for devious behaviour.
items.cn: 英语用 indirect 形容弯曲的路与不坦荡的行为。

items.en: Grammar adopted it for reported speech in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 语法学在十八世纪用它指转述话语。

items.en: Economics and lighting added the senses of shifted cost and reflected light.
items.cn: 经济学与照明又添上转嫁费用与反射光线之义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the direct root; the near-meaning group holds words for winding or roundabout.
note.cn: 形近组共用 direct 词根；近义组收表示迂回绕行的词。

entries.definition: Going straight or said plainly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「直接的」，去掉 in- 即成。

entries.definition: In a roundabout way.
The way something goes.
Long and not direct.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「绕路的、迂回的」。

entries.definition: Bending repeatedly along its length.
Understood without being said.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「暗示的、含蓄的」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the road around the hill, the plain-speaking contrast and the grammar term.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借绕山的路、与直言相对的写法以及语法术语。

normal.en: In plus direct: the line is bent, but the destination may still be reached.
normal.cn: in 加 direct：直线被折弯，终点却仍能到。

normal.en: Direct speech quotes; indirect speech reports: one small word changes the whole grammar of a story.
normal.cn: 直接引语加引号，间接引语转述：一个小前缀改了整个句子的语法。

normal.en: An indirect route is often cheaper than a direct flight, the bend has a price.
normal.cn: 迂回航线常比直飞便宜，弯折自有其代价。

normal.en: Indirect lighting means the bulb faces a wall, and the wall does the shining.
normal.cn: 间接照明是灯泡对着墙，由墙来发光。

normal.en: Being indirect in speech is not lying, only asking the listener to walk one extra step.
normal.cn: 说话迂回不是撒谎，只是让听者多走一步。

abstract.en: Every direct line is a decision to ignore the landscape.
abstract.cn: 每条直线都是一项不顾地形的决定。

abstract.en: Indirection is how fragile systems survive shocks, by travelling around them.
abstract.cn: 迂回是脆弱系统躲过冲击的方式：绕过去。

abstract.en: Not saying a thing plainly is still a way of saying it.
abstract.cn: 不把话说直白，也仍然是在说。

examples.en: They took an indirect route through the mountains.
examples.cn: 他们走了一条翻山的迂回路线。

examples.en: The cause of the illness was indirect.
examples.cn: 病因是间接的。

examples.en: He gave an indirect answer to my question.
examples.cn: 他对我的问题含糊其辞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印地瑞克特」——印刷地图上标的路绕了一大圈，是间接的。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dirigere（使之笔直，源自 regere「引导」）→ indirectus；同根词有 direct、direction、director、erect。

sensesIntro.en: Indirect denies a straight line, and the bent line reappears in routes, in speech, in causes, in light and money, and finally in grammar.
sensesIntro.cn: indirect 否定一条直线，而这条被折弯的线又在路线、话语、因果、光线与开销，最后在语法中复现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road bending around a hill yet still reaching the village.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绕过小山的路，最终仍到村庄。

branches.en: ROUTE LINE: the journey takes a longer way.
branches.cn: 路线线：行程绕了更远的路。

branches.en: SPEECH LINE: the meaning travels around the words.
branches.cn: 话语线：意思绕开了字面。

branches.en: CAUSAL LINE: effect arrives through a middle thing.
branches.cn: 因果线：效果经由中间环节到达。

branches.en: PHYSICAL LINE: light and cost arrive from a surface.
branches.cn: 物理线：光与费用从表面传来。

branches.en: GRAMMAR LINE: the voice of another is passed on.
branches.cn: 语法线：把别人的话转述出去。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning to guide straight, with a participial adjective ending.
intro.cn: 一个否定前缀加在意为「引导成直线」的词根上，再接分词形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus dirigere, to set straight, plus -ectus gave indirectus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 dirigere「使之笔直」加 -ectus，构成 indirectus。

definition_en: the scientific study of crime, criminals and the reasons behind them
core_image: 研究者把城市地图铺满墙面，用红点标出一桩桩案件
scene: 研究者在墙上铺开城市地图，用红点标出案件。 Criminology tries to explain why crime clusters in certain streets.
sceneCN: 这里 criminology 指「犯罪学」（第 1 个义项：把犯罪当作社会事实来研究的学科）；句意是犯罪学试图解释犯罪为何集中在某几条街上。

senses.title: The study of crime
senses.definition: the scientific study of crime as a fact of society
senses.definitionCN: 把犯罪当作社会事实来研究的学科
senses.example: Criminology asks why some streets are safer than others.
senses.exampleCN: 犯罪学追问为什么有些街道比另一些更安全。
senses.why: A repeated act can be counted, compared and explained.
senses.whyCN: 反复发生的行为可以被计数、比较和解释。

senses.title: The study of offenders
senses.definition: the part of the field that studies the people who commit crimes
senses.definitionCN: 这一领域中研究犯罪者本人的部分
senses.example: Criminology looks at the history of repeat offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 犯罪学考察惯犯的过往经历。
senses.why: Behind each act stands a person with a story.
senses.whyCN: 每一桩行为背后，都站着一个有故事的人。

senses.title: Research applied to policy
senses.definition: the use of such research in policing, courts and prevention
senses.definitionCN: 把这类研究用于警务、法庭与预防
senses.example: Modern criminology shapes how cities guard their streets.
senses.exampleCN: 现代犯罪学影响着城市如何守护街道。
senses.why: Knowledge of causes is useless until it changes a decision.
senses.whyCN: 对成因的认识，直到能改变决定时才有用。

intro.en: Criminology joins Latin crimen, a charge, with Greek -logia, the study of.
intro.cn: criminology 把拉丁语 crimen（指控）与希腊语 -logia（研究）拼在一起。

items.en: Crimen meant a charge or an accusation.
items.cn: crimen 意为指控或罪名。

items.en: Logos meant word, reason or account.
items.cn: logos 意为言说、理性或说明。

items.en: The suffix -logia named a field of study.
items.cn: 后缀 -logia 指一门研究领域。

items.en: Criminology was coined for the new science of crime.
items.cn: criminology 被造出来，命名这门新兴的犯罪科学。

items.en: Universities opened departments of criminology.
items.cn: 各大学开设了犯罪学系。

items.en: It now studies causes and prevention, not only acts.
items.cn: 今天它研究成因与预防，而不只是行为本身。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crimin- stem, and the meaning group names neighbouring fields of study.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crimin- 词干，近义组列出相邻的研究领域。

entries.definition: a person who has broken the law
an act that breaks the law
a person who studies crime
the study of punishment and prisons
entries.definitionCN: 研究刑罚与监狱的学问

entries.definition: the science used to examine evidence
the study of society and its groups
entries.definitionCN: 研究社会及其群体的学科

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a red dot on a map to a change in police policy.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地图上的一个红点，走到警务政策的一次改变。

normal.en: Crime plus -ology: the study of the act and its reasons.
normal.cn: crime 加 -ology：研究这一行为及其原因。

normal.en: A red dot is a story that has not been told yet.
normal.cn: 一个红点，就是一个还没讲出来的故事。

normal.en: Criminology counts patterns, not excuses.
normal.cn: 犯罪学数的是规律，不是借口。

normal.en: Every number on the map was once a person.
normal.cn: 地图上的每个数字，都曾是一个人。

normal.en: A theory earns its keep only when a street gets safer.
normal.cn: 理论只有在街道变安全时才算有用。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of maps pinned with red marks.
abstract.cn: 想象一整墙地图，钉满红点。

abstract.en: Picture a file that grows longer each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一份一年比一年厚的档案。

abstract.en: Picture a patrol route redrawn after a report.
abstract.cn: 想象一份报告之后被重画的巡逻路线。

examples.en: She took a degree in criminology.
examples.cn: 她取得了犯罪学学位。

examples.en: Criminology studies why crime rises in cities.
examples.cn: 犯罪学研究城市犯罪为何上升。

examples.en: Modern criminology often informs police policy.
examples.cn: 现代犯罪学常为警务政策提供依据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 criminology 记成 crime（罪行）加 -ology（学科）：研究罪行的学问，就是犯罪学。

root: 由拉丁语 crimen（指控、罪行）与希腊语 -logia（研究）合成；字面意思就是「对罪行的研究」，19 世纪起成为一门独立学科。

sensesIntro.en: From studying the act, to studying the person, to changing the policy.
sensesIntro.cn: 从研究行为，到研究人，再到改变政策。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a city map covered with red dots.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张钉满红点的城市地图。

branches.en: Counting the act turns crime into a visible pattern.
branches.cn: 把行为数出来，犯罪就变成看得见的规律。

branches.en: The people behind the acts become a subject of study.
branches.cn: 行为背后的人，成了研究的对象。

branches.en: Findings leave the desk and enter the police station.
branches.cn: 研究结论离开书桌，走进警局。

branches.en: Numbers and life stories are read side by side.
branches.cn: 数字与人生故事被并排阅读。

branches.en: Knowing offenders helps design better prevention.
branches.cn: 了解犯罪者，有助于设计更好的预防。

intro.en: Criminology is built from a Latin noun and a Greek suffix, joined in the 19th century.
intro.cn: criminology 由一个拉丁名词和一个希腊后缀拼成，成形于 19 世纪。

latinIntro.en: Crimen, a charge, supplies the stem crimin-; Greek -logia supplies the frame.
latinIntro.cn: crimen（指控）提供 crimin- 词干，希腊语 -logia 提供框架。

items.example: Criminology grew into a full subject.
items.exampleCN: 犯罪学发展成了一门完整学科。
这位犯罪学家把数据画成图。

items.meaning: relating to the study of crime
items.exampleCN: 这项调查用了犯罪学方法。

items.example: The crime was reported at once.
items.exampleCN: 这桩罪行立刻被报了案。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the law

items.example: The study compared criminality by area.
items.exampleCN: 研究比较了各区域的犯罪状况。
新证据使司机显得有罪。
有几个州把这一行为除罪化了。

latinEntries.example: The Latin crimen named the charge itself.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 crimen 指的正是那项指控。

definition_en: used to say that something is certainly true
core_image: 问题一出口，全场没有一个摇头的人
scene: 讲座结束时，主持人问在场有没有人反对这个结论，礼堂里安静了几秒，没有人举手。 This is undoubtedly the best solution available.
sceneCN: 这里 undoubtedly 是「毫无疑问」（第 1 个义项：表达确定无疑）；句意为这无疑是目前最好的办法。全场无人摇头，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的形容词，义为「无疑的；公认的」
同源形容词，义为「怀疑的；可疑的」

senses.title: Beyond any doubt
senses.definition: used to state that something is certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 用于表明某事确实成立
senses.example: The bridge is undoubtedly the finest in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥无疑是这一带最好的。
senses.why: The adverb is un- plus doubt plus -ed plus -ly, a stack of four pieces saying not doubted at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 un-、doubt、-ed、-ly 四层叠成，意思就是「一点也没被怀疑」。

senses.title: Used as a hedge in careful writing
senses.definition: used to soften a strong claim while keeping it firm
senses.definitionCN: 用来在保持坚持的同时稍微软化断言
senses.example: Undoubtedly, some details will change.
senses.exampleCN: 显然，有些细节会变。
senses.why: Formal writers like a small pause before the claim, and the adverb supplies it without weakening the claim.
senses.whyCN: 正式写作者喜欢在断言前留一小顿，这个副词在不减弱断言的前提下提供了那一顿。

senses.title: Used for emphasis on a prediction
senses.definition: placed before will to strengthen a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 放在 will 之前加强预测
senses.example: Prices will undoubtedly rise again.
senses.exampleCN: 价格必然会再次上涨。
senses.why: A forecast has no evidence in the present, so the word lends it borrowed certainty.
senses.whyCN: 预测在当下没有证据，这个词便借给它一份确定。

senses.title: Used for emphasis before a superlative
senses.definition: placed before a superlative to confirm the ranking
senses.definitionCN: 放在最高级前确认这一排名
senses.example: She is undoubtedly the most patient of the three.
senses.exampleCN: 她无疑是三人中最有耐心的。
senses.why: A superlative already claims the top, and the adverb confirms that nobody will dispute it.
senses.whyCN: 最高级本身已占住顶端，这个副词只是确认无人会提出异议。

senses.title: In the manner of something not doubted
senses.definition: of a fact, in a way that nobody questions
senses.definitionCN: 就某事实而言，无人质疑地
senses.example: His courage was undoubtedly real.
senses.exampleCN: 他的勇气无疑是真实的。
senses.why: The strength always sits in the doubting that is being denied.
senses.whyCN: 力量始终来自被否定掉的那份怀疑。

intro.en: The word is a four-part English stack on a Latin verb of doubting.
intro.cn: 这个词是四层英语叠加，底座是拉丁语的「怀疑」动词。

items.en: Dubitare means to waver between two things, related to duo, two.
items.cn: dubitare 意为在两者之间摇摆，与 duo（二）相关。

items.en: Old French douter carries the sense of fearing and questioning.
items.cn: 古法语 douter 带出「畏惧、存疑」之义。

items.en: Doubt enters English, and the adjective undoubted adds un- to deny it.
items.cn: doubt 进入英语后，形容词 undoubted 加 un- 加以否认。

items.en: The adverb undoubtedly is formed with -ly and becomes frequent in formal prose.
items.cn: 副词 undoubtedly 加 -ly 而成，在正式文章中频繁出现。

items.en: Modern usage often places it at the start of a sentence as a confident opener.
items.cn: 现代用法常把它放在句首，作为有把握的开场。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the doubt family, and the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of certainty.
note.cn: 形近组共用 doubt 词族，近义组汇集表示确定的副词。

entries.definition: a feeling of not being sure
unsure or unlikely
not questioned
without any doubt
in a clear and sure way
possibly, as can be argued
maybe

normalIntro.en: Un- denies the doubt, -ed frames it as a settled fact, and -ly makes it an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: un- 否定怀疑，-ed 把它说成既成事实，-ly 再把它变成副词。

normal.en: Dubitare means to waver between two things, so undoubted means no wavering at all.
normal.cn: dubitare 意为在两者间摇摆，undoubted 就是完全不摇摆。

normal.en: Undoubtedly and undoubtedly true are both common, the second adding emphasis.
normal.cn: undoubtedly 与 undoubtedly true 都常见，后者再加一层强调。

normal.en: In careful writing it softens a claim without giving it up.
normal.cn: 在严谨写作里它软化断言，却不放弃断言。

normal.en: Before will and before a superlative it works as a firm support.
normal.cn: 放在 will 与最高级之前，它起稳固的支撑作用。

normal.en: The adjective form undoubted is rarer but appears in formal prose.
normal.cn: 形容词形式 undoubted 较少用，但见于正式文章。

abstract.en: Ask a room for objections and watch no hand go up.
abstract.cn: 向一屋子人问有没有异议，看没有一只手举起来。

abstract.en: Hear the pause that grows heavier than any answer.
abstract.cn: 听那阵沉默比任何回答都更沉。

abstract.en: Then place that certainty in front of a claim and walk away.
abstract.cn: 再把这份确定放在一句论断前面，转身走开。

examples.en: The discovery is undoubtedly important for farmers.
examples.cn: 这一发现对农民无疑很重要。

examples.en: She is undoubtedly the strongest player in the team.
examples.cn: 她无疑是队里最强的选手。

examples.en: The news will undoubtedly spread by morning.
examples.cn: 这消息到早上必然会传开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的闹特得利」——心里安，闹不清楚的（not）东西都理得利落，自然无疑。

root: un-（否定）+ doubt（拉丁语 dubitare「摇摆不定」，与 duo「二」同源）+ -ed + -ly；现多作副词 undoubted + -ly

sensesIntro.en: One meaning at bottom: the doubt that would normally be there is not there.
sensesIntro.cn: 归根到底只有一个意思：本该出现的怀疑并未出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question asked and no hand raised.
core.cn: 核心意象：问题问出，无人举手。

branches.en: The certain branch: a plain statement of fact.
branches.cn: 确定分支：对事实的平实陈述。

branches.en: The hedge branch: softening a claim without dropping it.
branches.cn: 缓和分支：软化而不放弃。

branches.en: The forecast branch: certainty about the future.
branches.cn: 预测分支：对未来的确定。

branches.en: The ranking branch: confirming a superlative.
branches.cn: 排序分支：确认最高级。

branches.en: The everyday use before a plain adjective.
branches.cn: 接普通形容词的日常用法。

intro.en: Four English layers over a Latin verb of wavering.
intro.cn: 四层英语部件叠在一个拉丁语「摇摆」动词上。

latinIntro.en: Dubitare also lies behind dubious and doubt.
latinIntro.cn: dubitare 还支撑着 dubious 与 doubt。

items.example: She was doubtful of the plan.

items.exampleCN: 她无可置疑的技艺令我们佩服。

definition_en: using numbers stored as electronic signals, especially in computers
core_image: 一块屏幕亮起，无数小方格排成图案，每个格子只有亮与不亮
scene: 老人把胶片相机收进抽屉，换了一台薄薄的机器。 All the photos are now stored in digital form.
sceneCN: 这里 digital 指「数字的」（第 1 个义项：以数字信号记录）；句意是如今所有照片都以数字形式保存。

senses.title: Stored as numbers
senses.definition: recorded as a series of numbers that a machine can read
senses.definitionCN: 被记录成一串机器能读的数字
senses.example: The signal is converted into digital form.
senses.exampleCN: 信号被转换成数字形式。
senses.why: A smooth wave is cut into steps that a chip can count.
senses.whyCN: 平滑的波被切成格子，芯片才数得清。

senses.title: Built around such signals
senses.definition: describing devices and services that work with such signals
senses.definitionCN: 形容依靠这类信号运转的设备与服务
senses.example: The digital camera fits in a coat pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 这台数码相机能塞进外套口袋。
senses.why: The product is named after the kind of signal inside it.
senses.whyCN: 产品是照着它内部那种信号来命名的。

senses.title: Relating to a finger
senses.definition: relating to a finger or a toe in medical use
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指与手指或脚趾有关
senses.example: The surgeon repaired a digital nerve.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生修复了一根手指神经。
senses.why: The oldest sense comes from counting on the fingers.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的那层意思，来自扳着手指计数。

intro.en: Digital comes from Latin digitus, a finger, because people once counted on their fingers.
intro.cn: digital 来自拉丁语 digitus（手指），因为人最早是扳着手指计数的。

items.en: Digitus meant a finger or a toe.
items.cn: digitus 指手指或脚趾。

items.en: The same word named a numeral, since fingers were the first counters.
items.cn: 同一个词也指数目，因为手指是最早的算具。

items.en: English digit meant a number below ten.
items.cn: 英语 digit 指十以下的数字。

items.en: Digital described anything done with a finger.
items.cn: digital 形容任何用手指完成的事。

items.en: Electronics gave the word its current sense of number-coded signals.
items.cn: 电子技术让它有了今天「数字编码信号」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the digit- stem, while the meaning group covers numbers, electronics and two-state coding.
note.cn: 形近组共用 digit 词干，近义组则覆盖数值、电子与两态编码。

entries.definition: one of the numbers from zero to nine
the quality of deserving respect
to turn information into numbers
expressed by numbers
working with tiny electric circuits
using only two states, such as on and off
entries.definitionCN: 只用通与断这两种状态的

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with fingers used for counting and end with a screen of on and off cells.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从数数的手指开始，最后落到一块只有亮与不亮的屏幕。

normal.en: Digit is a finger first and a number second.
normal.cn: digit 先是手指，后才是数字。

normal.en: Ten fingers gave us ten digits, and digits gave us digital.
normal.cn: 十根手指给出十个数字，数字又给出 digital。

normal.en: Digital sound is a wave cut into tiny stairs.
normal.cn: 数字声音是被切成小台阶的波。

normal.en: A digital photo is a grid of numbers pretending to be light.
normal.cn: 数码照片是一格数字假装成光。

normal.en: Before screens, digital meant done with a finger.
normal.cn: 在有屏幕之前，digital 只表示用手指做的事。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding up three fingers to count.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起三根手指在数数。

abstract.en: Picture a waveform chopped into equal steps.
abstract.cn: 想象一条波形被切成等高的台阶。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of cells where each is either lit or dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一片方格，每一格要么亮，要么暗。

examples.en: Most music is now sold in digital form.
examples.cn: 如今大多数音乐以数字形式出售。

examples.en: The digital clock lost a minute every month.
examples.cn: 这台数字钟每个月慢一分钟。

examples.en: Older workers often fear the digital age.
examples.cn: 年长的工人常常害怕数字时代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 digital 记成「地记头」：地上一格一格记下来，数字排好，就是数码。

root: 来自拉丁语 digitus（手指）。人最早扳手指计数，所以同一个词也指数目，英语 digit 便指零到九的数字。二十世纪电子技术用「只有通与断两种状态」的方式记录信息，digital 因此获得今天「数字的、数码的」这层含义，而医学上仍保留「手指的」原义。

sensesIntro.en: From counting on fingers, to a signal counted by a chip, to the devices built on that signal, and back to the finger itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从扳手指计数，到芯片数得出的信号，到靠这种信号运转的设备，最后回到手指本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grid of cells, each either lit or dark, forming a picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片方格，每格或亮或暗，凑成一幅图。

chain: A CHIP READS ON AND OFF

branches.en: The first sense is the coded signal itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那串被编码的信号。

branches.en: The second sense names the machines built on it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项指靠它运转的机器。

branches.en: The third sense returns to the body part.
branches.cn: 第三个义项回到身体部位。

branches.en: The signal and the device share one adjective.
branches.cn: 信号与设备共用同一个形容词。

branches.en: The newest sense and the oldest both trace back to fingers.
branches.cn: 最新的意思与最老的意思，都能追回到手指。

intro.en: Digital belongs to the digit- family, running from fingers to numbers to machine code.
intro.cn: digital 属于 digit 一族，从手指一路走到数字，再到机器编码。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin digitus, a finger, which also gave the word for a numeral.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 digitus（手指），它同时给出了「数字」这个词。

items.exampleCN: 这批档案已全部数字化。

items.example: Write the answer as a single digit.
The form can be signed digitally.
They digitize old tapes each winter.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年冬天把旧磁带数字化。

items.meaning: the act of converting to numbers
items.exampleCN: 数字化抢救了那些易碎的地图。
数字化改变了整个办公室。

items.meaning: a plant named for its finger-shaped flowers
items.example: Digitalis is used in small doses.
items.exampleCN: 毛地黄只以小剂量入药。

definition_zh: 寡妇；遗孀；使成为寡妇；独占（口语）
definition_en: a woman whose husband has died and who has not married again, and the verb of making her so
core_image: 一间只摆着一把椅子的空屋，窗台上还放着两个人的照片
scene: 村里那位老妇人自从丈夫走后，就一直一个人守着院子里那把旧椅子。 The widow next door still keeps two chairs on her porch.
sceneCN: 这里 widow 是「寡妇」（第 1 个义项：丈夫去世后没有再婚的妇女）；句意为隔壁的寡妇仍在门廊上放着两把椅子。只摆一把椅子的空屋，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A woman whose husband died
senses.definition: a woman who has lost her husband by death and has not married again
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫去世后没有再婚的妇女
senses.example: The widow next door still keeps two chairs on her porch.
senses.exampleCN: 隔壁的寡妇仍在门廊上放着两把椅子。
senses.why: The noun is one of the oldest words for a person left alone by death, and it has almost no figurative life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是最古老的、指因死亡而独留一人的名词之一，几乎不带比喻用法。

senses.title: The male counterpart
senses.definition: used in the phrase widow and widower, the pair naming the two sides of the same loss
senses.definitionCN: 用于 widow and widower 这一对照说法，指同一损失的男女两面
senses.example: The law then spoke of widows but said nothing of widowers.
senses.exampleCN: 那时的法律只提到寡妇，对鳏夫只字未提。
senses.why: The newer form widower was made by adding -er to match other pairs such as speaker and listener.
senses.whyCN: 较晚出现的 widower 是加 -er 造出来的，以与 speaker、listener 等成对词语对齐。

senses.title: To make someone a widow
senses.definition: in older or formal use, to take away a person s partner by death
senses.definitionCN: 旧式或正式用法，指因死亡而使某人失去配偶
senses.example: War widowed thousands of women in a single decade.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间，战争使成千上万的女性成为寡妇。
senses.why: A noun became a verb because English likes to turn a state into an act.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成了动词，因为英语喜欢把状态转写成动作。

senses.title: A short last line of a paragraph
senses.definition: in printing, a single short line at the top of a page left from the previous paragraph
senses.definitionCN: 印刷排版中，上一段遗留在页面顶部的一行孤零零的文字
senses.example: The editor closed the widow at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把页首那行孤立的字收了回来。
senses.why: A printers term borrowed it because the line stands alone at the top of a page, like someone left behind.
senses.whyCN: 印刷术语借用了这个词，因为那行字孤零零立在页顶，像被留下的人。

senses.title: In card games and informal use
senses.definition: in card games, an extra hand dealt to players, and in casual speech to be left without a partner
senses.definitionCN: 牌戏中指额外补发的手牌，口语中指被撇下没有搭档
senses.example: We were three, so one player had to sit out as the widow.
senses.exampleCN: 我们是三个人，只好让一位当没搭档的那个。
senses.why: The metaphor of being left alone travelled into games and into jokes about odd numbers.
senses.whyCN: 「被留下」的比喻进入了牌戏，也进入了关于人数的玩笑。

intro.en: Widow descends from Old English widewe, from a Germanic root meaning empty or separated, related to the Latin vidua.
intro.cn: widow 源自古英语 widewe，其日耳曼语词根意为「空的、被分开的」，与拉丁语 vidua 同源。

items.en: The root carried the idea of being bereft or empty, the state rather than the person.
items.cn: 这个词根带有「被夺走、空着」之意，强调状态而非人。

items.en: Widewe named a woman left without a husband, and the word carried legal weight in land claims.
items.cn: widewe 指失去丈夫的女性，这个词在土地归属中带有法律分量。

items.en: The form shifted to widwe and then widow, and the endings simplified.
items.cn: 词形先后变为 widwe 与 widow，词尾也随之简化。

items.en: Widower was coined by adding -er, completing a pair the older language had left unpaired.
items.cn: widower 是加 -er 造出来的，补齐了旧语言未曾成对的一面。

items.en: The word also entered printing and card games, where something stands alone at the top.
items.cn: 这个词也进入印刷与牌戏，用来指孤零零立在顶部的东西。

note.en: The first group gathers the family words that pair with widow, the second the words about loss and being left alone.
note.cn: 第一组收与 widow 成对的家族词，第二组收表示失去与独留的词。

entries.definition: A man whose wife has died, the male pair.
Having lost a husband or wife.
The state of being a widow.
An opening in a wall, one letter away.
A child whose parents have died.
Not married, but not because of death.
The adjective used for either sex.

normalIntro.en: Widow only differs from window by two letters, and the two are the usual source of confusion.
normalIntro.cn: widow 与 window 只差两个字母，两者是最常见的混淆源。

normal.en: A widow is a woman left, a widower is a man left, and the -er marks the man.
normal.cn: widow 是被留下的女人，widower 是被留下的男人，-er 标记男性。

normal.en: Window has an n, widow has none.
normal.cn: window 里有个 n，widow 里没有。

normal.en: The old root meant empty, which is why the word describes a state.
normal.cn: 古老的词根意为「空」，所以这个词描述的是状态。

normal.en: A war widow is a fixed collocation that appears in history books.
normal.cn: war widow 是历史书里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Printing calls a lone line a widow, alone at the top of a page.
normal.cn: 印刷业把页顶孤立的一行也叫 widow。

abstract.en: See one chair on a porch left empty.
abstract.cn: 看见门廊上留下的一把空椅子。

abstract.en: Feel a room that is still arranged for two.
abstract.cn: 感觉一间仍按两个人摆放的房间。

abstract.en: Hear a name spoken in the past tense.
abstract.cn: 听见一个用过去时被提起的名字。

examples.en: The widow runs the shop that her husband opened.
examples.cn: 这位寡妇经营着丈夫开的那家店。

examples.en: Many women were widowed during the long war.
examples.cn: 漫长的战争让许多女性成了寡妇。

examples.en: She has been a widow for nearly twenty years.
examples.cn: 她守寡将近二十年了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「微多」——一个人微微多了些孤单，所以是寡妇。

root: 日耳曼语词根（空、被分开）→ 古英语 widewe → 中古英语 widow → 现代英语 widow；同族有 widower、widowed、widowhood。

sensesIntro.en: The word names a woman left by death, gives her a male pair, turns into the act of causing that state, and finally lends itself to a lone line on a page.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先命名因死亡而独留的女性，再配出男性一面，随后转成造成这种状态的动作，最后借给页面上孤立的一行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chair still standing where two once stood.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该两把椅子并排，却只剩一把。

branches.en: The woman branch: two chairs on the porch.
branches.cn: 女性分支：门廊上的两把椅子。

branches.en: The pair branch: law that spoke only of widows.
branches.cn: 成对分支：只说寡妇的法律。

branches.en: The verb branch: war widowing thousands.
branches.cn: 动词分支：战争使成千上万人丧偶。

branches.en: The printing branch: a lone line at the top.
branches.cn: 排版分支：页首孤立的一行。

branches.en: The games branch: one player without a partner.
branches.cn: 牌戏分支：没有搭档的那一位。

intro.en: Widow is a root word, and its small family is built with -er, -ed and -hood rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: widow 是词根词，它的小词族靠 -er、-ed、-hood 扩展，而不用前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Germanic root is distantly related to Latin vidua, which gives the English adjective vidual and the word viduity.
latinIntro.cn: 这个日耳曼语词根与拉丁语 vidua 有远亲关系，后者给出英语的 vidual 与 viduity。

items.meaning: a woman bereft of her husband
items.example: It works as noun and verb.
The possessive marks the older legal style.
items.exampleCN: 所有格标示旧式法律文体。

items.meaning: to lose a partner by death
items.example: The passive avoids naming the cause.

items.meaning: a historic phrase for a young widow
items.example: It names a social wrong of the past.
items.exampleCN: 它指认过去的一种社会弊端。

latinEntries.example: It is the direct Latin cousin of the Germanic word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是这个日耳曼词在拉丁语中的直接表亲。

latinEntries.example: It shows the old idea of emptiness.

definition_en: unfair treatment of a group of people, or the ability to see fine differences
core_image: 两张几乎一样的简历被推向桌子两边，一边的椅子却更高
scene: 两叠简历内容几乎一样，却被推向了不同的方向。 She spoke out against discrimination in hiring.
sceneCN: 这里 discrimination 指「歧视」（第 1 个义项：因群体身份而受的不公平对待）；句意是她公开反对招聘中的歧视。

senses.title: Unfair treatment of a group
senses.definition: the unfair treatment of people because of their group, age or sex
senses.definitionCN: 因所属群体、年龄或性别而受到的不公平对待
senses.example: The law forbids discrimination at work.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止职场歧视。
senses.why: A line is drawn first, and then one side is given less.
senses.whyCN: 先画一道线，然后让一边少拿。

senses.title: The power to tell things apart
senses.definition: the ability to see small differences between things
senses.definitionCN: 看出事物之间细微差别的能力
senses.example: Good tea needs a fine discrimination of smell.
senses.exampleCN: 懂好茶需要精细的嗅觉辨别力。
senses.why: The same sharp eye that separates can also sort people unfairly.
senses.whyCN: 能分辨的锐利眼光，也可能被用来不公平地分流人群。

intro.en: Discrimination comes from Latin discriminare, to divide or separate, from discrimen, a dividing line.
intro.cn: discrimination 来自拉丁语 discriminare（分开、区分），其根 discrimen 指分界线。

items.en: Discrimen meant a line that separates two things.
items.cn: discrimen 指把两样东西分开的界线。

items.en: Discriminare meant to divide or to distinguish.
items.cn: discriminare 指划分或加以区别。

items.en: English used it for the act of telling differences.
items.cn: 英语借入后指辨别差异的行为。

items.en: The sense of unfair treatment by group grew in law and politics.
items.cn: 按群体不公平对待这一义项在法律与政治中长出来。

items.en: Both the sharp eye and the closed door keep the same word.
items.cn: 敏锐的眼光与关上的门，共用这一个词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the discrimin- stem, and the meaning group names unfair attitudes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 discrimin- 词干，近义组列出几种不公平的态度。

entries.definition: to see a difference or to treat unfairly
entries.definitionCN: 分辨差异或加以不公平对待

entries.definition: able to judge fine differences
done without any choice or care
a leaning that makes judgement unfair
an opinion formed before the facts
entries.definitionCN: 未看事实就形成的看法

entries.definition: the quality of not being just

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a chalk line and end with a hand that can weigh two shades.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道粉笔线开始，落到一只能掂量两种色差的手。

normal.en: Discrimin- means to separate; -ion makes it a practice.
normal.cn: discrimin- 是分开，-ion 把它变成一种做法。

normal.en: A line drawn around a group soon becomes a wall.
normal.cn: 围着某个群体画下的线，很快会变成墙。

normal.en: The same word praises a fine palate and blames a closed door.
normal.cn: 同一个词既夸精细的品味，也指责关上的门。

normal.en: Discrimination at work can hide inside a polite rule.
normal.cn: 职场歧视能藏在一条规定里。

normal.en: A discriminating reader notices the missing sentence.
normal.cn: 有辨别力的读者看得出少掉的那一句。

abstract.en: Picture one line of chalk across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面上划过一道粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture two identical files placed at different heights.
abstract.cn: 想象两份一样的档案被放在不同高度。

abstract.en: Picture an eye that can weigh two almost equal colours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼能掂量两种几乎相同的颜色。

examples.en: The company was sued for discrimination.
examples.cn: 这家公司因歧视被起诉。

examples.en: She has a fine discrimination of taste and smell.
examples.cn: 她对味道与气味有精细的辨别力。

examples.en: Age discrimination is hard to prove.
examples.cn: 年龄歧视很难证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discrimination 记成「划线分开」：discrimin- 是划分，-ion 是行为；把人按群体划开并少给，就是歧视；把事物细细划开，就是辨别力。

root: 源自拉丁语 discrimen（分界线）与 discriminare（划分、区别），进入英语后先指辨别差异，十九世纪起在法律与政治语境里指按群体给予不公平对待，于是同一个词兼有「辨别力」与「歧视」两面。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of drawing a line between things, to the unfair line drawn around people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从在事物之间划线，到围着人群划出的一条不公平的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chalk line across a table, with one side quietly given less.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌面上一道粉笔线，一边悄悄少拿了东西。

chain: THE LINE HARDENS INTO A WALL

branches.en: The first sense is the wall built around a group.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是围着某个群体砌起的墙。

branches.en: The second sense is the eye that can weigh fine shades.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是能掂量细微差别的眼睛。

branches.en: Both start from the same act of separating.
branches.cn: 两个义项都始于同一个分开的动作。

branches.en: Both need a line before anything can be sorted.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有线，才能分拣。

branches.en: Only the second sense is a skill worth training.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项是值得训练的本事。

intro.en: Discrimination belongs to the Latin discrimin- family, where separating and sorting share one root.
intro.cn: discrimination 属于拉丁语 discrimin- 一族，区分与分拣共用同一个根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin discrimen, a dividing line, gives discriminare and then discrimination in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discrimen（分界线）给出 discriminare，再进入英语成为 discrimination。

items.meaning: the act of separating or treating unfairly

items.example: The test discriminates between two groups.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试把两组人区分开。
这条规定被称为歧视性的。
她有一双有辨别力的耳朵。
这张网不加区分地捕鱼。

items.meaning: the practice of not treating people unfairly
a thing that separates one from another

definition_en: the floor of a ship; also a set of playing cards
core_image: 船头被浪打湿的木板
scene: 海风很大，水手们沿着木板上上下下地跑。 The sailors stood on the deck and watched the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 deck 指「甲板」（第 1 个义项：船上的木板层）；句意是水手们站在甲板上看风暴。

senses.title: The floor of a ship
senses.definition: the flat floor of a ship or a boat
senses.definitionCN: 船只上平整的那层地面
senses.example: The sailors stood on the deck and watched the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 水手们站在甲板上看风暴。
senses.why: A ship needs one plain surface where work and weather meet.
senses.whyCN: 船需要一块平整的表面，让劳作与风雨在这里相遇。

senses.title: A complete set of cards
senses.definition: the full set of cards used for a game
senses.definitionCN: 供游戏使用的一整套纸牌
senses.example: He shuffled the deck and dealt four hands.
senses.exampleCN: 他洗了牌，发了四手。
senses.why: Fifty-two cards stacked as one object get a single name.
senses.whyCN: 五十二张牌叠成一件东西，就该有一个名字。

senses.title: To decorate
senses.definition: to hang things on something to make it festive
senses.definitionCN: 把东西挂上去，使某处显得喜庆
senses.example: They decked the hall with paper flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用纸花装饰了大厅。
senses.why: A bare surface is dressed the way a ship is fitted out.
senses.whyCN: 光秃的表面被装点，和船被装备起来是一个道理。

intro.en: Deck came from Middle Low German dek, a covering or roof, from decken, to cover.
intro.cn: deck 来自中古低地德语 dek（覆盖物、屋顶），源于 decken（遮盖）。

items.en: Dek meant a covering or a roof.
items.cn: dek 指覆盖物或屋顶。

items.en: Dec named the covering planks laid over a ship's beams.
items.cn: dec 指铺在船梁上的那层木板。

items.en: Deck entered English as the top floor of a ship.
items.cn: deck 作为船的最上层进入英语。

items.en: To deck meant to cover or dress something.
items.cn: 动词 deck 指把东西覆盖、装点起来。

items.en: A deck of cards names a stacked set lying on a table.
items.cn: a deck of cards 指桌上叠好的一整套牌。

note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音，近义组则分别对应地面、一整套和装饰。

entries.definition: a table used for writing or working

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从脚下湿漉漉的木板开始，落到墙上的一串纸花。

normal.en: To deck a room is to dress it for a day.

abstract.en: Picture a wave breaking over the front planks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个浪打在前面的木板上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand cutting a full set of cards.

abstract.en: Picture a bare hall turned bright with paper flowers.

examples.en: The sailors stood on the deck and watched the storm.
examples.cn: 水手们站在甲板上看风暴。

examples.en: He dealt a card from the top of the deck.

examples.en: They decked the room with lights for the party.

root: 来自中古低地德语 dek（覆盖物、屋顶），动词 decken 意为遮盖。荷兰语里它先指铺在船梁上的木板，十五世纪进入英语成为「甲板」；十六世纪又生出「装点、覆盖」的动词义，后来一整套叠好的纸牌也被叫作一副牌。

sensesIntro.en: From the planks under a sailor's feet, to a stacked set of cards, to a surface dressed for a party.
sensesIntro.cn: 从水手脚下的木板，到叠好的一整套牌，再到为聚会装点起来的表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet wooden planks underfoot on a moving ship.
core.cn: 核心意象：晃动船上脚下那层湿木板。

branches.en: The first sense is the covering that makes a ship walkable.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是让船能走人的那层铺面。

branches.en: The second sense is a covering stacked into one neat set.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是叠成一整套的覆盖物。

branches.en: The third sense turns covering into decorating.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把「覆盖」变成了「装点」。

branches.en: A ship is fitted out and a hall is dressed by the same idea.
branches.cn: 船被装备好、厅被装点好，用的是同一个念头。

branches.en: Stacking and spreading are two ways of putting one thing over another.
branches.cn: 叠起来和铺开来，都是把一件东西放到另一件上面。

intro.en: Deck forms compounds on ships and at parties: deckhand, deckchair, decking.
intro.cn: deck 在船上和聚会上都组词：deckhand、deckchair、decking。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here; the word is Low German in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁成分，它源自低地德语。

items.example: She bought a new deck of cards.

definition_zh: 宽容；容忍；忍耐力；公差；耐受力
definition_en: the willingness to accept behaviour or opinions different from your own, or the ability to endure something difficult without harm
core_image: 一个人把重物扛在肩上，压得弯了腰却没有把重物扔下去
scene: 师傅带着徒弟在车床边量一个轴，卡尺读数总比图纸大上一丝。 The machinist explained that a little tolerance is built into every part so that it will still fit.
sceneCN: 这里 tolerance 是机械加工中的「公差」（第 4 个义项：允许的尺寸偏差）；句意为师傅解释说每个零件都留了一点公差，这样才装得进去。画面里有车床、卡尺与图纸。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去掉后缀 -ance 构成动词，义为「容忍；忍受」
由动词加 -ant 构成形容词，义为「宽容的；能耐受的」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「宽容地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不宽容；不耐受」

senses.title: Willingness to accept differences
senses.definition: the quality of accepting opinions, beliefs, or customs that differ from one's own
senses.definitionCN: 接受与自己不同的观点、信仰或习俗的品质
senses.example: His tolerance of other faiths made him welcome in every village.
senses.exampleCN: 他对其他信仰的宽容使他在每个村子都受到欢迎。
senses.why: The word comes from a Latin verb meaning to bear or endure, and accepting difference is a way of bearing what is not ours.
senses.whyCN: 本词来自拉丁语中表示「承担、忍受」的动词，接受差异就是承担不属于自己的东西。

senses.title: The capacity to endure hardship
senses.definition: the ability to put up with pain, noise, or difficulty without breaking down
senses.definitionCN: 承受痛苦、噪音或困难而不垮掉的能力
senses.example: Years of field work had raised his tolerance for cold and hunger.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的野外工作提高了他对寒冷和饥饿的忍耐力。
senses.why: Bearing a load physically becomes bearing hardship mentally, so the same noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 身体上承担重量，自然转为精神上承担艰苦，同一个名词就兼指两者。

senses.title: Biological resistance to a substance
senses.definition: the body's ability to take a drug, poison, or food without harmful effects
senses.definitionCN: 身体服用药物、毒物或食物而不受伤害的能力
senses.example: Long use of the medicine can build up a tolerance, so the dose must be raised.
senses.exampleCN: 长期服用这种药会产生耐受性，因此剂量必须加大。
senses.why: A body that bears a substance without harm is literally enduring it, which is the oldest sense of the root.
senses.whyCN: 身体能承受某种物质而不受伤害，正是词根最古老意义上的「忍受」。

senses.title: Allowed variation in engineering
senses.definition: the amount by which a measurement may vary and still be acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 测量值允许变动而仍属合格的范围
senses.example: Each bolt is cut within a tolerance of a tenth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 每颗螺栓的切割都控制在十分之一毫米的公差内。
senses.why: A workshop bears a small error the way a person bears an annoyance, and this mechanical sense grew in the machine age.
senses.whyCN: 车间容忍一点误差，正如人容忍一点冒犯，这个机械义项是在机器时代长出来的。

senses.title: Open-mindedness in public life
senses.definition: a social attitude that lets unpopular views be expressed without punishment
senses.definitionCN: 允许不受欢迎的观点被表达而不受惩罚的社会态度
senses.example: The reform was praised as a step towards greater religious tolerance in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革被誉为该地区走向更大的宗教宽容的一步。
senses.why: When the capacity to bear extends beyond one person to a whole society, it becomes a public principle.
senses.whyCN: 当这种承受能力从一个人扩展到整个社会，它就成了公共原则。

senses.title: The margin allowed in a plan
senses.definition: a margin left in a budget, schedule, or system so that small problems do not ruin it
senses.definitionCN: 预算、进度或系统中预留的余地，使小问题不会毁掉全局
senses.example: We left a week of tolerance in the schedule for bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在日程里留了一周的余量以应对坏天气。
senses.why: A tolerance is always a space that can absorb a knock, whether in metal or in a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 公差永远是能吸收撞击的一块空间，无论它出现在金属里还是日程里。

senses.title: Refusal to forbid what one dislikes
senses.definition: the practice of allowing something one disapproves of rather than banning it
senses.definitionCN: 对自己不赞成的事不加禁止的做法
senses.example: Her tolerance of noisy neighbours did not mean she liked the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 她对吵闹邻居的容忍并不意味着她喜欢那种噪音。
senses.why: This sense stresses the negative side of bearing: not approving, merely not stopping.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调「承受」的否定面：并不赞同，只是没有制止。

senses.title: The limit of what can be borne
senses.definition: the point at which patience or endurance finally gives way
senses.definitionCN: 耐心或耐力最终崩溃的那一刻
senses.example: The crowd's tolerance broke when the third train was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 第三趟列车被取消时，人群的忍耐到了极限。
senses.why: Every tolerance has an edge, and naming the edge turns the noun into a measure of the breaking point.
senses.whyCN: 任何容忍都有边界，把边界说出来，这个名词就成了崩溃点的度量。

intro.en: The word goes back through French to Latin tolerare, to bear or put up with, a verb whose exact prehistory is debated but whose sense has stayed remarkably steady for two thousand years.
intro.cn: 本词经法语上溯到拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受），这个词动词的更深来源尚有争议，但其含义两千年来相当稳定。

items.en: Tolerare means to bear, endure, or put up with, and is used of carrying a load as well as of enduring a person.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tolerare 意为「承担、忍受」，既用于扛负重物，也用于忍受某个人。

items.en: The related adjective tolerabilis describes what can be borne, and the noun tolerantia names the bearing itself.
items.cn: 相关形容词 tolerabilis 表示「可以承受的」，名词 tolerantia 则指承受这件事本身。

items.en: Old French tolerance keeps the medical and moral senses of the Latin noun in the learned register.
items.cn: 古法语 tolerance 在书面语中保留了拉丁名词的医学与道德含义。

items.en: English borrows the word in the sixteenth century, first for the bearing of pain and then for the bearing of differences of creed.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入此词，先指忍受疼痛，继而指容忍教义上的差异。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the political sense of letting dissenting churches exist is well established.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，「允许异议教派存在」的政治含义已经完全确立。

items.en: Engineering takes the word up in the nineteenth century for the permitted error in a measurement, and the biological sense of drug tolerance follows in the twentieth.
items.cn: 工程学在十九世纪用它表示测量中允许的误差，二十世纪又出现药物耐受性这一生物学含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem, while the near-meaning group gathers terms for patience and for limits set in numbers.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在同一拉丁词干上的词，近义组则汇集表示耐心以及用数字设定的限度的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the Latin stem, from the common collocations, and from the word family built with -ant and -ate.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从拉丁词干、常用搭配以及用 -ant 和 -ate 构成的词族入手。

normal.en: Tolerare meant to carry a weight, so tolerance is a muscle that has learned to carry.
normal.cn: tolerare 意为扛重量，所以 tolerance 是一块学会负重的肌肉。

normal.en: Tolerate is the verb, tolerant the adjective, tolerance the noun: -ate, -ant, -ance.
normal.cn: tolerate 是动词，tolerant 是形容词，tolerance 是名词，后缀依次为 -ate、-ant、-ance。

normal.en: Zero tolerance is a policy phrase, and the zero shows that the limit has been set at nothing.
normal.cn: zero tolerance 是政策用语，那个零说明限度被设为零。

normal.en: In a workshop, tolerance is the small space that lets a metal part slide in instead of jamming.
normal.cn: 在车间里，公差是让金属件能滑进去而不是卡住的那点缝隙。

normal.en: Drug tolerance means the body has learned to carry the dose, so the dose must grow.
normal.cn: 药物耐受性指身体学会了扛住这个剂量，于是剂量必须增加。

abstract.en: Picture a porter with a crate on his back who does not set it down at the first step.
abstract.cn: 想象一名脚夫背着木箱，走第一步时并没有把它放下。

abstract.en: Think of a door frame made a millimetre too wide, and the door that never sticks.
abstract.cn: 想一个做宽了一毫米的门框，和一扇从此不再卡住的门。

abstract.en: Tolerance is a deliberately loose grip: tight enough to hold, loose enough to let air through.
abstract.cn: 容忍是一种故意放松的握法：紧到能握住，松到能让空气通过。

examples.en: The school teaches tolerance of different backgrounds.
examples.cn: 这所学校教导学生宽容不同的背景。

examples.en: Repeated use of the painkiller raised her tolerance to it.
examples.cn: 反复使用这种止痛药提高了她对它的耐受性。

examples.en: The parts are machined to a tolerance of one hundredth of a millimetre.
examples.cn: 这些零件被加工到百分之一毫米的公差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托了忍死」——托着、忍着，忍到死也不松手，就是容忍。

root: 拉丁语 tolerare（承担、忍受）→ tolerantia（忍受）→ 古法语 tolerance → 英语 tolerance。同族词有 tolerate、tolerant、tolerable；词根更深层的来源，一般认为与「举起、支撑」一类词形有关，但尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: From the single image of bearing a load, the entry spreads outwards: bearing other people, bearing pain, bearing a drug, and finally the measured margin that lets metal or schedules absorb a knock.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「承受重量」这一个意象出发，本词向外展开：承受他人、承受痛苦、承受药物，最后是让金属或日程吸收撞击的那段可量度的余量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load carried on the shoulders without dropping it.
core.cn: 核心意象：肩上的重物被一直扛着，没有放下。

branches.en: Bearing other people and their differences.
branches.cn: 承受他人及其差异。

branches.en: Bearing hardship, and the moment the bearing fails.
branches.cn: 承受艰苦，以及承受失灵的那一刻。

branches.en: Bearing a substance inside the body.
branches.cn: 身体内部承受某种物质。

branches.en: Bearing a measured error in a machine.
branches.cn: 承受机器上可量度的误差。

branches.en: Bearing a knock in time, money, or plans.
branches.cn: 在时间、金钱或计划中承受意外撞击。

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb stem with the noun ending -ance, and its family is formed with -ate, -ant, -able, and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: 本词由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀 -ance 构成，同族词由 -ate、-ant、-able 与否定前缀 in- 构成。

definition_en: to burst with great force; to show strong emotion suddenly; to increase very quickly
core_image: 封闭的东西突然炸开，碎片四散
scene: 旧锅炉在深夜突然爆炸。 The old boiler exploded suddenly late at night.
sceneCN: 这里 explode 是「爆炸」（第 1 个义项）；句意：旧锅炉在深夜突然爆炸。

senses.title: Burst with force
senses.definition: to burst with great force and noise
senses.definitionCN: 伴随巨大力量和声响炸开
senses.example: The gas tank exploded without warning.
senses.exampleCN: 气罐毫无征兆地爆炸了。
senses.why: The core sense is a violent burst.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是猛烈的炸开。

senses.title: Burst with emotion
senses.definition: to show strong emotion suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然表现出强烈情绪
senses.example: She exploded with anger at the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，她勃然大怒。
senses.why: A physical burst becomes an emotional one.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的炸开变成情绪上的爆发。

senses.title: Grow very fast
senses.definition: to increase very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 非常迅速地增长
senses.example: The city's population exploded after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后这座城市的人口激增。
senses.why: Sudden bursting becomes sudden growth.
senses.whyCN: 突然炸开变成突然增长。

intro.en: Explode comes from Latin explodere, to drive off by clapping.
intro.cn: explode 源自拉丁语 explodere，意为「用掌声把…轰下去」。

items.en: Explodere joins ex- (out) with plaudere (to clap).
items.cn: explodere 由 ex-（向外）与 plaudere（拍手）构成。

items.en: It first means to hiss an actor off stage.
items.cn: 它最初指用嘘声把演员轰下台。

items.en: Explode is used for driving something out.
items.cn: explode 用于表示把某物赶出去。

items.en: Explode gains the sense of bursting out.
items.cn: explode 获得「炸开」的含义。

items.en: Explode also describes rapid growth.
items.cn: explode 还用于描述快速增长。

note.en: Explode is to blow up; explore is to search a place.

normalIntro.en: Explode is a sudden burst of force, feeling, or growth.
normalIntro.cn: explode 是力量、情绪或增长上的突然爆发。

normal.en: The fireworks exploded above the river.
normal.cn: 烟花在河面上空炸开。

normal.en: He exploded when he heard the lie.
normal.cn: 听到那个谎言，他爆发了。

normal.en: Online sales exploded during the holiday.
normal.cn: 节日期间线上销售猛增。

normal.en: The old tyre could explode if overfilled.
normal.cn: 旧轮胎充气过满可能爆裂。

normal.en: The report aims to explode a popular myth.
normal.cn: 这份报告旨在打破一个流行迷思。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed paper bag bursting all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密封纸袋一下子胀破。

abstract.en: Imagine a volcano waking after years of sleep.
abstract.cn: 想象沉睡多年的火山突然醒来。

abstract.en: Think of a crowded room breaking into noise.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤的房间突然喧闹起来。

examples.en: A fuel pipe exploded under the road.
examples.cn: 一条燃料管道在路面下爆炸了。

examples.en: The audience exploded into applause at the end.
examples.cn: 结尾时观众爆发出掌声。

examples.en: Demand for the device exploded after the review.
examples.cn: 评测发布后，这款设备的需求猛增。

sensesIntro.en: Explode means to burst with force, to burst out with emotion, or to grow very fast.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed thing breaking open outward.

branches.en: The burst becomes explosive growth.

branches.en: Physical and emotional bursts share suddenness.
branches.cn: 物理爆炸与情绪爆发都强调突然。

branches.en: Blowing up and shooting up both escalate fast.
branches.cn: 炸开与猛增都是迅速升级。

definition_en: in a way that is intended to be hidden from others
core_image: 门缝里透出一线灯光，有人正把箱子悄悄推到床底下
scene: 他趁家人睡下，悄悄把礼物藏进衣柜。 He secretly hid the gift in the wardrobe.
sceneCN: 这里 secretly 是「秘密地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他偷偷把礼物藏进衣柜。

senses.title: In a hidden way
senses.definition: in a manner kept hidden from other people
senses.definitionCN: 以对他人隐藏的方式
senses.example: They secretly planned a surprise party.
senses.exampleCN: 他们秘密策划了一场惊喜派对。
senses.why: This is the general adverb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是该副词的宽泛义。

senses.title: Without being noticed
senses.definition: doing something without other people noticing
senses.definitionCN: 在别人没有察觉的情况下做某事
senses.example: The letter was secretly copied.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信被偷偷复印了。
senses.why: The focus shifts from secrecy to avoiding notice.
senses.whyCN: 重点从保密转向避免被发现。

senses.title: Within one's heart
senses.definition: felt privately without being expressed
senses.definitionCN: 私下怀有而不表达出来
senses.example: He secretly hoped she would stay.
senses.exampleCN: 他暗自希望她会留下。
senses.why: Private feeling is another kind of hiddenness.
senses.whyCN: 私下的情感是另一种隐藏。

intro.en: Secretly is secret with the adverb suffix -ly, from Latin secretus.
intro.cn: secretly 是 secret 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，secret 源自拉丁语 secretus。

items.en: Secretus meant hidden or set apart.
items.cn: secretus 意为隐藏的或分开的。

items.en: Secret named something kept from view.
items.cn: secret 表示被藏起来的事物。

items.en: Secret entered English as noun and adjective.
items.cn: secret 作为名词和形容词进入英语。

items.en: The adverb secretly formed with -ly.
items.cn: 副词 secretly 由 -ly 构成。

items.en: Secretly now covers hidden action and private feeling.
items.cn: 现代英语中 secretly 涵盖隐秘行动与私下情感。

note.en: Secretly is compared with similar-looking words and with words for privacy.
note.cn: 把 secretly 与形近词以及表示私下、隐秘的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Secretly means doing, keeping, or feeling something out of others' sight.
normalIntro.cn: secretly 意为在他人视线之外做、藏或感受某事。

normal.en: Secretly is secret plus -ly.
normal.cn: secretly 由 secret 加 -ly 构成。

normal.en: Secretly plan means plan without telling.
normal.cn: secretly plan 意为不告知地策划。

normal.en: Secretly hope is a private feeling.
normal.cn: secretly hope 是私下里的愿望。

normal.en: Secretly record raises questions of consent.

normal.en: The word ends in -ly like most adverbs.

core.en: Acting or feeling outside the view of others.

definition_en: a machine with a wheel that is spun by steam, gas or water in order to produce power
core_image: 水流冲击一圈金属叶片，轮轴在轰鸣中飞速旋转
scene: 水坝底部的机房里，水从高处冲下来，推动一整排金属轮子。 Each turbine in the plant can light a small town.
sceneCN: 这里 turbine 是「涡轮机」（第 1 个义项：靠蒸汽、燃气或水流冲转轮子来产生动力的机器）；句意为厂里每台涡轮机都能照亮一座小镇。水流冲击叶片、轮轴狂转的画面，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 turbine 附近的词干构成，义为「陀螺状的」
由 turbine 加 driven 构成，义为「涡轮驱动的」
turbine 的缩略形式，义为「涡轮；涡轮增压器」

senses.title: The spinning wheel
senses.definition: a machine whose wheel is turned by a moving fluid, changing that motion into power
senses.definitionCN: 靠流动的流体带动轮子旋转、把转动变成动力的机器
senses.example: Each turbine in the plant can light a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 厂里每台涡轮机都能照亮一座小镇。
senses.why: The name points at the wheel itself, the part that turns.
senses.whyCN: 词名直指那个轮子，那个真正在转的部件。

senses.title: The engine built around it
senses.definition: a whole engine, as in a jet, that works by driving such a wheel
senses.definitionCN: 如喷气机中围着一个涡轮工作的整台发动机
senses.example: The aircraft is fitted with a new turbine.
senses.exampleCN: 这架飞机装有新型涡轮发动机。
senses.why: Because the wheel is the heart of the engine, the part name came to stand for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 轮子是发动机的心脏，于是部件的名字代替了整体。

intro.en: Turbine was coined in the nineteenth century from the Latin word for a whirl, turbinis.
intro.cn: turbine 是十九世纪用拉丁语中表示「漩涡」的词 turbinis 造出来的。

items.en: Turbo meant a whirl or a spinning top, and its genitive turbinis named the whirling thing.
items.cn: turbo 意为漩涡或陀螺，其属格 turbinis 命名旋转之物。

items.en: French engineers used the Latin stem in the vocabulary of early hydraulic machinery.
items.cn: 法国工程师在早期水力机械的词汇里用上了这个拉丁词干。

items.en: In the eighteen twenties the word was given to a wheel spun by water.
items.cn: 十九世纪二十年代，这个词被赋予被水流冲转的轮子。

items.en: Steam engines then used turbines for a far greater spinning force.
items.cn: 蒸汽机随后用涡轮机取得大得多的旋转力。

items.en: Jets and power stations made it an everyday word for a machine that whirls.
items.cn: 喷气机与电站使它成为「旋转的机器」的日常用词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin whirl, the second names power machines.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「旋转」词根，第二组是动力机器的名称。

entries.definition: A turbine or a turbocharger.
Rough, unsettled movement.
To break someone's calm.
A machine that produces motion.
A machine that makes electricity.

normalIntro.en: Turbine and turbulence come from the same Latin whirl, so the machine is a tame tempest.
normalIntro.cn: turbine 与 turbulence 同出拉丁语的「旋转」，所以这台机器是一头被驯服的旋风。

normal.en: The second syllable carries the stress in British speech: TUR-bine.
normal.cn: 英式发音重音多在第二音节。

normal.en: Turbine shares its stem with disturb and turbulence.
normal.cn: turbine 与 disturb、turbulence 共享词干。

normal.en: A turbine turns a flow of fluid into a turn of the shaft.
normal.cn: 涡轮机把流体的流动变成轴的转动。

normal.en: Turbo is the clipped, faster form of the same word.
normal.cn: turbo 是同一个词的缩略快读形式。

normal.en: Nothing spins without blades, so picture the blades first.
normal.cn: 没有叶片什么也转不起来，先想叶片。

abstract.cn: 一圈叶片接住一股水柱。

abstract.en: A whirlpool seen from above, frozen in metal.
abstract.cn: 从上方看去的漩涡，凝在金属里。

abstract.en: The low hum of a hall full of spinning wheels.
abstract.cn: 一屋子里满是转轮的低声轰鸣。

examples.en: Wind turbines line the ridge above the village.
examples.cn: 风力涡轮机排在小村上方的山脊上。

examples.en: A damaged turbine can cut the station's output by half.
examples.cn: 一台受损的涡轮机能让电站发电量减半。

examples.en: The turbine spins thousands of times a minute.
examples.cn: 这台涡轮机每分钟转几千次。

sensesIntro.en: First the spinning wheel, then the whole engine built around that wheel.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是那个在转的轮子，再是围着这个轮子造出的整台发动机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water striking a ring of blades.
core.cn: 核心意象：水撞上一圈叶片。

branches.en: The wheel branch: fluid turned into spin.
branches.cn: 轮子分支：流体变为旋转。

branches.en: The engine branch: the whole machine takes the part's name.
branches.cn: 发动机分支：整体借用了部件的名字。

branches.en: The power branch: spin becomes electricity.

branches.en: The flight branch: a jet rides on its turbines.
branches.cn: 飞行分支：喷气机靠涡轮飞行。

intro.en: Turbine is a Latin stem with a noun ending, and its relatives cluster around the idea of whirling.
intro.cn: turbine 是带名词词尾的拉丁词干，其亲属词都围绕「旋转」聚拢。

latinIntro.en: Latin turbo and its family supplied several English words about disturbing and whirling.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 turbo 及其词族贡献了若干表示搅动与旋转的英语词。

definition_zh: 松散地；不紧地；宽大地；不严格地；大致地
definition_en: in a way that is not tight or close, not fitting closely, or not strictly and precisely
core_image: 一件宽大的外套松松地搭在椅背上，两只袖子垂下来
scene: 排练室里，几个人站得很开，动作只是大致跟着节拍。 The dancers moved loosely, as if the music were only a suggestion.
sceneCN: 这里 loosely 是「松散地、不严格地」（第 3 个义项：不严格、大致地）；句意为舞者动作松散，好像音乐只是建议。图中可辨识物件：排练室、舞者、节拍。

pos.zh: 松散地；不紧地；宽大地；不严格地；大致地

derivatives.zh: 由词基 loose 加 -en 构成，义为「松开；放宽」，与 loosely 共享词根
由 loose 加 -ness 构成，义为「松弛；松散」，与 loosely 同族
由 loose 与 fitting 复合，义为「宽松的」，描述与 loosely 相近的版型

senses.title: In a way that is not tight
senses.definition: with little tension, so that something can move or slip
senses.definitionCN: 张力很小，因此某物可以移动或滑动
senses.example: She tied the rope loosely around the post.
senses.exampleCN: 她把绳子松松地系在柱子上。
senses.why: The adverb takes the adjective's physical slackness and turns it into the manner of an action: the hand does not pull hard.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把形容词的物理松弛转成动作的方式：手没有用力去拉。

senses.title: In a way that does not fit closely
senses.definition: of clothing, worn so that it hangs away from the body
senses.definitionCN: 指衣服穿着时离开身体、垂下来
senses.example: He wore his coat loosely over his shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 他把外套松松地披在肩上。
senses.why: Loose cloth hangs; the adverb describes how the garment sits, so fit becomes the second branch.
senses.whyCN: 宽松的布料会垂下来；副词描述衣服如何罩在身上，于是「合身程度」成为第二条分支。

senses.title: Not strictly or precisely
senses.definition: without exact limits, so that the meaning is approximate rather than exact
senses.definitionCN: 没有精确的界限，因此含义是大致的，而非准确的
senses.example: The film is loosely based on a true story.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影大致根据一个真实故事改编。
senses.why: When rules or facts are not pinned down, the manner of holding them is the same as holding a rope without pulling it tight.
senses.whyCN: 当规则或事实没有被钉死，握住它们的方式就像握着一根没有拉紧的绳子。

senses.title: In a loose or unconnected structure
senses.definition: of a group, text or arrangement, with parts not closely joined or ordered
senses.definitionCN: 指群体、文本或安排中的各部分没有紧密连接或排列
senses.example: The chapters are loosely connected by a single theme.
senses.exampleCN: 各章只由一条单一的主题松散地串起来。
senses.why: Parts that are not bound together stay separate; the adverb describes the gaps between them rather than the tightness of any one part.
senses.whyCN: 没有被捆在一起的部分保持分离；副词描述的是它们之间的空隙，而不是某一部分本身有多紧。

intro.en: Loosely is an English adverb made from loose plus -ly; the base word is Germanic, and its senses move from slack rope to inexact description.
intro.cn: loosely 是由 loose 加 -ly 构成的英语副词；词基属于日耳曼语族，义项从松弛的绳子走向不精确的描述。

items.en: The base adjective is generally traced to Old Norse lauss, meaning slack or free.
items.cn: 词基形容词一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss，意为松的、自由的。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic source also gives German los and the English suffix -less.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语来源也给出德语 los 与英语后缀 -less。

items.en: Middle English used loos or loose as an adjective before the adverb was formed.
items.cn: 在副词形成之前，中古英语已用 loos 或 loose 作形容词。

items.en: The adverb suffix -ly descends from Old English -lice, and loosely appears as loose plus that suffix.
items.cn: 副词后缀 -ly 源自古英语 -lice，loosely 就是 loose 加上这个后缀。

items.en: Modern English extends the adverb from the manner of tying to the accuracy of a claim, so loosely based on becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词从系绳的方式扩展到陈述的准确程度，于是 loosely based on 成为常见说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective, verb and noun of the same family plus the confusing lose; the near-meaning group gathers words for approximation and slackness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形容词、动词与名词，外加容易混淆的 lose；近义组收表示近似与松弛的词。

entries.definition: Not tight, not fitting closely, or free from restraint.
entries.definitionCN: 词基形容词兼动词，义为「松的；宽松的；不受约束的」。

entries.definition: To make or become less tight.
entries.definitionCN: 同族动词，义为「使变松；松开」。

entries.definition: The quality or state of being loose.
entries.definitionCN: 同族名词，义为「松弛；松散」。

entries.definition: To no longer have something, or to fail to keep it.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写和读音相近，词源不同；义为「丢失；失去」。

entries.definition: Approximately, without exact detail.
entries.definitionCN: 大致地；强调近似，不强调松紧。

entries.definition: Close to a number or amount but not exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 大约；强调数量接近，用于数字与测量。

entries.definition: With little tension or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 松弛地；强调张力不足，多用于绳索、肌肉或管理。

entries.definition: In a relaxed or informal way.

normalIntro.en: The word is loose plus the old adverb suffix -ly, and its family keeps returning to light grips, loose fit and inexact limits.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 loose 加上古老的副词后缀 -ly，同族词反复回到轻轻的握持、宽松的版型与不精确的界限。

normal.en: Loosely is loose plus -ly, so the adverb keeps the adjective's idea of something not held tight.
normal.cn: loosely 是 loose 加 -ly，所以这个副词保留了形容词「没有被紧紧握住」的意思。

normal.en: Tie a rope loosely and it can slip; state a rule loosely and it can be read in more than one way.
normal.cn: 绳子系得松会滑；规则说得松，就可能被读出不止一种意思。

normal.en: Loosely based on is the standard phrase for a film or book that changes many details of its source.
normal.cn: loosely based on 是电影或书改编时改动许多细节的标准说法。

normal.en: Loosen is the verb of the family, loosely the adverb, looseness the noun.
normal.cn: 这一词族里，loosen 是动词，loosely 是副词，looseness 是名词。

normal.en: Lose is only a look-alike; it means to no longer have something and has nothing to do with slackness.
normal.cn: lose 只是形近词；它表示不再拥有某物，与松弛无关。

abstract.en: A loosely woven fabric holds air between its threads, which is why loose structures are both weaker and more open.
abstract.cn: 织得松的布料在纱线之间留住空气，所以松散的结构既更脆弱，也更开阔。

abstract.en: A loosely worded promise leaves room for escape, and room for escape is exactly what the word describes.
abstract.cn: 措辞松散的承诺留有退路，而「留有余地」正是这个词所描述的东西。

abstract.en: Loosely does not mean carelessly; it means the grip is light enough to let the thing breathe.
abstract.cn: loosely 并不等于粗心；它说的是握得够轻，能让那东西透气。

examples.en: The dancers moved loosely, as if the music were only a suggestion.
examples.cn: 舞者动作松散，好像音乐只是建议。

examples.en: The film is loosely based on a true story.
examples.cn: 这部电影大致根据一个真实故事改编。

examples.en: She tied the rope loosely around the post.
examples.cn: 她把绳子松松地系在柱子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「露斯利」——衣服松松散散地挂着，走起路来还带着晃；loosely 就是松散地。

root: loose（松的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；loose 一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss（松的、自由的），属日耳曼语族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is action done without tightness; the senses divide into slack tying, loose fit, inexact claims and weakly joined parts.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是不带紧绷感的动作；义项由此分出系得松、穿得宽、说法不精确，以及各部分连接松散。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide coat hanging loosely from the back of a chair, its sleeves drooping.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件宽大的外套松松地搭在椅背上，两只袖子垂下来。

branches.en: a rope tied without pulling it tight
branches.cn: 绳子系上却没有拉紧

branches.cn: 外套松松地离开肩膀垂着

latinIntro.en: Loosely is an English adverb built on loose; the base word has Germanic rather than Latin origins, so no Latin family is listed.

senses.definition: a substance from a plant used to flavour food

items.en: The spice trade made it a word of wealth.

items.en: It came to mean anything that adds interest.

definition_zh: 毫克（千分之一克）；按毫克计的药量；极微的含量
definition_en: a unit of mass equal to one thousandth of a gram, and by extension a dose or a trace amount measured in that unit
core_image: 天平上一小撮白色粉末，指针几乎不动，刻度只轻轻跳了一格
scene: 药房里，穿白大褂的人把一片小药丸放到精密天平上，显示屏上的数字小得要用放大镜才看得清。 The label says each tablet contains only a few milligrams of the active ingredient.
sceneCN: 这里是「毫克」（第 1 个义项：千分之一克的质量单位）；句意为标签标明每片药只含少量有效成分的毫克数。图中可辨识物件：白大褂、药丸、精密天平、被放大的显示屏。

derivatives.zh: 英式旧拼写，与 milligram 同义，仍见于较早的药品说明书
由希腊语 gramma 经法语 gramme 进入英语，义为「克」，是毫克所依据的基本单位
把前缀 milli- 换成 micro-（百万分之一），义为「微克」，比毫克再小一千倍

senses.title: One thousandth of a gram
senses.definition: a unit of mass in the metric system, equal to one thousandth of a gram
senses.definitionCN: 公制中量质量的一个单位，等于一克的千分之一
senses.example: The pharmacist weighed out four milligrams of the powder.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师称出了四毫克粉末。
senses.why: The prefix milli- is Latin mille, a thousand, and gram is the base unit of mass; the name states its own size outright, one thousandth of a gram, so the unit sense is the arithmetic core the other senses grow from.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 milli- 来自拉丁语 mille（千），gram 是质量的基本单位，名字一拼起来就把大小说清楚了：一克的千分之一。所以「单位」这一层是整词的算术内核，其余用法都从这里往外长。

senses.title: A dose strength written in milligrams
senses.definition: the amount of a drug or nutrient stated in milligrams on a prescription, packet or label
senses.definitionCN: 处方、药盒或标签上用毫克标明的药物或营养成分含量
senses.example: The doctor lowered her daily dose by five milligrams.
senses.exampleCN: 医生把她的每日剂量减少了五毫克。
senses.why: A strong drug works in thousandths of a gram, so a prescription needs a unit fine enough to separate a helpful amount from a harmful one; the milligram became the natural word for the figure printed on the packet.
senses.whyCN: 强效药的有效量与危险量常常只差千分之几克，处方需要一个细到能分开「有用」和「有害」的单位，毫克于是成了药盒上那个数字的日常说法。

senses.title: A faint trace measured in the same unit
senses.definition: a very small quantity, counted in milligrams, found by careful testing in food, water or a sample
senses.definitionCN: 在食物、水或样品中经仔细检测才发现的极少量，以毫克计
senses.example: Testing found only milligrams of copper in the tap water.
senses.exampleCN: 检测发现自来水里只有几毫克铜。
senses.why: Minerals in food and water sit far below the scale of a gram, so labels and lab reports drop a thousandfold and count in milligrams; here the unit measures what a thing contains rather than what a person takes.
senses.whyCN: 食物和水里的矿物质远不到一克，标签与检验报告便下降一千倍、用毫克来点数；这时同一个单位量的是「某物里有什么」，而不是「一个人吃多少」。

intro.en: Milligram is a modern coinage of the metric system: a Latin prefix for a thousandth joined to a Greek word for a small weight, passed through French before it reached English.
intro.cn: milligram 是公制时代的近代造词：表示千分之一的拉丁前缀，接上希腊语中「小重量」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Mille was the Latin numeral for a thousand and gave the prefix milli-, which shrinks a unit to its thousandth.
items.cn: mille 是拉丁语的「千」，由此得到前缀 milli-，把一个单位缩小到它的千分之一。

items.en: Greek gramma first meant a written mark and later a small weight; French took it as gramme, the base unit of mass.
items.cn: 希腊语 gramma 最初指写下的记号，后来指小重量；法语取作 gramme，作为质量的基本单位。

items.en: French scientists coined milligramme while the metric system was being built in the late eighteenth century, joining milli- directly to gramme.
items.cn: 十八世纪末建立公制时，法国学者把 milli- 直接拼到 gramme 上，造出 milligramme。

items.en: English adopted the word as milligram in the nineteenth century, as metric measures spread through pharmacies, laboratories and trade.
items.cn: 十九世纪，随着公制进入药房、实验室与贸易，英语把这个词收作 milligram。

items.en: Modern usage keeps milligram for prescriptions, food labels and trace reports, where thousandths of a gram are ordinary working figures.
items.cn: 现代用法把 milligram 留在处方、食品标签与痕量报告里，千分之一克在那里是寻常的工作数字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers spellings and units built on the same two building blocks; the near-meaning group gathers words for amounts and for old measures of mass.
note.cn: 形近组收由同样两个构件拼成的拼写与单位；近义组收表示「量」以及旧式质量单位的词。

entries.definition: An older British spelling of the same unit, still met in dated medical texts.
entries.definitionCN: 同一单位的英式旧拼写，仍见于较早的医学文本。

entries.definition: The base metric unit of mass, one thousand times larger than a milligram.
entries.definitionCN: 公制质量的基本单位，比毫克大一千倍。

entries.definition: A unit one thousandth of a milligram, used for vitamins and hormones.
entries.definitionCN: 比毫克再小一千倍的单位，用于维生素与激素。

entries.definition: A unit of volume built with the same milli- prefix, so it measures space rather than mass.
entries.definitionCN: 同用 milli- 前缀的体积单位，量的是空间而不是质量。

entries.definition: The amount of a medicine taken at one time, often stated in milligrams.
entries.definitionCN: 一次服用的药量，常以毫克表示。

entries.definition: An amount so small that only careful measurement can show it.
entries.definitionCN: 小到只有仔细测量才能显现的量。

entries.definition: An old unit of mass still used for bullets and medicines, about sixty-five milligrams.
entries.definitionCN: 仍用于子弹与药物的旧质量单位，约合六十五毫克。

entries.definition: A larger everyday unit of mass, equal to about twenty-eight grams.
entries.definitionCN: 日常使用的较大质量单位，约合二十八克。

normalIntro.en: The word is assembled from a prefix that means a thousandth and a base unit, and its family keeps returning to small measured amounts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示千分之一的前缀和一个基本单位拼成，同族词反复回到「被量出来的小量」。

normal.en: Milli- is Latin for a thousandth and gram is the base unit, so the word needs no story once the two parts are known.
normal.cn: milli- 表示千分之一，gram 是基本单位，认识这两块，词义就不必再讲故事。

normal.en: A gram is about the weight of a paper clip, so a milligram is that clip cut into a thousand slivers too small to see.
normal.cn: 一克大约是一枚回形针的重量，一毫克就是把它切成一千片看不见的细屑。

normal.en: Prescriptions print milligrams because the gap between help and harm in a strong drug is often a few thousandths of a gram.
normal.cn: 处方上印毫克，是因为强效药「有效」与「有害」之间常常只差几千分之一克。

normal.en: Food labels count iron, sodium and vitamins in milligrams, since a meal holds these minerals far below a gram.
normal.cn: 食品标签用毫克标注铁、钠与维生素，因为一顿饭里这些矿物质的量远不到一克。

normal.en: Microgram is the next step down, one thousandth of a milligram, built simply by swapping milli- for micro-.
normal.cn: microgram 再往下一级，是毫克的千分之一，构词上只是把 milli- 换成 micro-。

abstract.en: A unit too small to move a kitchen scale is the one that decides whether a medicine heals or harms.
abstract.cn: 一个在厨房秤上毫无反应的单位，却决定了药是救人还是伤人。

abstract.en: Figures that look like dust on a screen still carry the full weight of a decision about a human body.
abstract.cn: 屏幕上像灰尘一样的数字，仍背着关于一个人身体的整个决定。

abstract.en: The word names its own size, and that honesty is exactly what makes it trusted in a laboratory.
abstract.cn: 这个词把自己的大小写在名字里，这份坦白正是它在实验室里被信任的原因。

examples.en: The recipe calls for two milligrams of the colouring agent.
examples.cn: 配方要求加入两毫克着色剂。

examples.en: The daily dose was reduced to fifty milligrams.
examples.cn: 每日剂量被降到五十毫克。

examples.en: Only a milligram of the mineral remains in each litre.
examples.cn: 每升水里只剩下了一毫克这种矿物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米粒」——milli 听起来像「米粒」，一克分成一千份，每份小得像一粒米；记住 milligram 是毫克。

root: 拉丁语 mille（千）派生前缀 milli-（千分之一），接希腊语 gramma（小重量）经法语 gramme，合成法语 milligramme，十九世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The arithmetic unit comes first; the other senses take that same tiny scale to the pharmacy counter and then to the food label and the water report.
sensesIntro.cn: 先立住那个算术意义上的单位；其余义项把同一把极小的尺子带到药房柜台，再带到食品标签与水质报告。

core.cn: 核心意象：天平上一小撮白色粉末，指针只轻轻挪动一格。

branches.cn: 天平为一小撮粉末只挪动一格

branches.en: a prescription printed in figures smaller than a grain of salt
branches.cn: 处方上印着比盐粒还小的数字

branches.cn: 护士把药片对半切，削去几毫克

branches.en: a nutrition label read through a magnifying glass
branches.cn: 隔着放大镜读营养成分表

branches.cn: 水质报告里标出一种含量极微的金属

intro.en: The word stands on a Latin numeral for a thousand, a Greek word for a small weight, their French combination, and English endings that name the unit and its smaller relatives.

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the numeral for a thousand and the ordinal for a thousandth, the two forms that make the metric prefix possible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示「千」的数词与表示「第一千」的序数词，正是这两个形式使公制前缀得以成立。
