core_image: 孩子们在花园里笑着奔跑
scene: 孩子们在花园里快乐地玩耍。 The children played happily in the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 happily 是「快乐地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们在花园里快乐地玩耍。

senses.title: With joy
senses.definition: in a way that shows happiness
senses.definitionCN: 以表现快乐的方式
senses.example: The children played happily in the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在花园里快乐地玩耍。
senses.why: The plain adverb of happy is the base sense.
senses.whyCN: happy 最直接的副词义，是基础义项。

senses.title: By good luck
senses.definition: fortunately, when something good happens by chance
senses.definitionCN: 幸运的是，好事碰巧发生
senses.example: Happily, no one was hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 幸运的是，没有人受伤。
senses.why: Happy once meant lucky, and the adverb keeps it.
senses.whyCN: happy 早期意为幸运，副词保留了这层意思。

senses.title: Willingly
senses.definition: willingly and with pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 愿意且愉快地
senses.example: I will happily help you.
senses.exampleCN: 我很乐意帮你。
senses.why: Joy in a task becomes willingness to do it.
senses.whyCN: 做事的愉快，变成了做事的意愿。

intro.en: Happily is happy plus -ly; happy comes from hap, chance or luck.
intro.cn: happily 由 happy 加 -ly 构成；happy 来自 hap（偶然、运气）。

items.en: Happ meant chance or good luck.
items.cn: happ 意为偶然或好运。

items.en: Happy first meant lucky or fortunate.
items.cn: happy 最初意为幸运的。

items.en: Happy came to mean glad or pleased.
items.cn: happy 转而意为高兴的、满意的。

items.en: Happily added the adverb ending -ly.
items.cn: happily 加上副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: It kept both the joy and the luck senses.
items.cn: 它同时保留了快乐与幸运两层意思。

note.en: Happily is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of joy.
note.cn: 把 happily 与形近词以及表示喜悦的副词作比较。

entries.definition: feeling pleasure
to take place
the state of being happy
with great joy
willingly and with pleasure
in good spirits

normalIntro.en: Happily is with joy, by good luck, or with a willing heart.
normalIntro.cn: happily 是带着喜悦、凭着好运，或怀着乐意的心。

normal.en: The children played happily in the garden.
normal.cn: 孩子们在花园里快乐地玩耍。

normal.en: Happily, no one was hurt.
normal.cn: 幸运的是，没有人受伤。

normal.en: I will happily help you.
normal.cn: 我很乐意帮你。

normal.en: They lived happily for many years.
normal.cn: 他们幸福地生活了许多年。

normal.en: She happily agreed to the plan.
normal.cn: 她欣然同意了这个计划。

abstract.en: Joy is a way of walking, not only a feeling.
abstract.cn: 快乐不只是一种感觉，也是一种走路的姿态。

abstract.en: Good luck is joy that arrives without asking.
abstract.cn: 好运，是不请自来的快乐。

abstract.en: A willing yes is already half the work done.
abstract.cn: 乐意的「好」，已经是完成一半的工作。

examples.en: The children played happily in the garden.
examples.cn: 孩子们在花园里快乐地玩耍。

examples.en: Happily, no one was hurt.
examples.cn: 幸运的是，没有人受伤。

examples.en: I will happily help you.
examples.cn: 我很乐意帮你。

dict_mnemonic.text: happily 由 happy 加 -ly 构成，意为「快乐地」，也指「幸运地」和「乐意地」；happily ever after 是童话结尾的幸福生活。

root: 由 happy（快乐的，源自 hap 运气）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；由幸运引申出的快乐，扩展为快乐地、幸运地与乐意地。

sensesIntro.en: Happily means with joy, fortunately, or willingly.
sensesIntro.cn: happily 指快乐地、幸运地，或乐意地。

core.en: A joyful way of doing something.
core.cn: 带着喜悦做事的姿态。

branches.en: Children run laughing in a garden.
branches.cn: 孩子们笑着在花园里跑。

branches.en: A fall ends without injury.
branches.cn: 一跤摔下却没有受伤。

branches.en: A helper says yes at once.
branches.cn: 帮忙的人立刻答应。

branches.en: Joy and good luck can wear the same face.
branches.cn: 快乐与好运，可以戴着同一张脸。

branches.en: Joy in doing becomes willingness to do.
branches.cn: 做事的快乐，变成做事的意愿。

intro.en: Happily builds on happy with -ly, and happy forms comparison.
intro.cn: happily 由 happy 加 -ly 构成，happy 又能构成比较级。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; hap comes from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，hap 来自古诺斯语。

definition_en: a series of things coming one after another, or the act of taking over a position
core_image: 一排人依次走上传送带，一个接一个
scene: 一连串的暴风雨袭击了海岸。 A succession of storms hit the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 succession 是「一连串」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一连串的暴风雨袭击了海岸。

senses.title: Series
senses.definition: a number of things or events coming one after another
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个出现的事物或事件
senses.example: A succession of storms hit the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一连串的暴风雨袭击了海岸。
senses.why: This is the common sense of a long series.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示长长一串的常用义项。

senses.title: Inheritance
senses.definition: the act of taking over an office or a title
senses.definitionCN: 接任职位或头衔的行为
senses.example: The succession to the throne was peaceful.
senses.exampleCN: 王位继承过程很和平。
senses.why: One ruler follows another into the same seat.
senses.whyCN: 一位统治者跟着另一位坐上同一个位置。

senses.title: In a row
senses.definition: one after another without a break
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个，中间没有间断
senses.example: She won three races in succession.
senses.exampleCN: 她接连赢了三场比赛。
senses.why: The phrase in succession stresses no pause between events.
senses.whyCN: 短语 in succession 强调事件之间没有停顿。

intro.en: Succession comes from Latin words for following after.
intro.cn: succession 来自拉丁语，本义是跟在后面。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or to give way.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让路。

items.en: Succedere meant to come after.
items.cn: succedere 意为随后而来。

items.en: Successio meant a following after.
items.cn: successio 意为随后跟随。

items.en: Succession meant a following in order.
items.cn: succession 意为按顺序跟随。

items.en: Succession meant taking over an office.
items.cn: succession 意为接任职位。

items.en: Succession also means a series of events.
items.cn: succession 也指一连串事件。

note.en: Succession is compared with look-alike words and with words for series.
note.cn: 把 succession 与形近词以及表示序列的词作比较。

entries.definition: following one after another
a person who takes over
a period of an activity
a number of similar things in order
things following in a fixed order
the receiving of a position or property

normalIntro.en: Succession is a line of things, each stepping into the last place.
normalIntro.cn: succession 就是一条队伍，每个都接上前一个的位置。

normal.en: A succession of storms hit the coast.
normal.cn: 一连串的暴风雨袭击了海岸。

normal.en: The succession to the throne was peaceful.
normal.cn: 王位继承过程很和平。

normal.en: She won three races in succession.
normal.cn: 她接连赢了三场比赛。

normal.en: He faced a succession of small problems.
normal.cn: 他面对一连串小问题。

normal.en: The line of succession was never clear.
normal.cn: 继承顺序一直不明确。

abstract.en: A succession of days makes a life.
abstract.cn: 一连串的日子，组成了一生。

abstract.en: Every throne is a succession of borrowed seats.
abstract.cn: 每张王座，都是一连串借来的座位。

abstract.en: We inherit more than we succeed to.
abstract.cn: 我们继承的东西，比我们接替的位置更多。

examples.en: A succession of storms hit the coast.
examples.cn: 一连串的暴风雨袭击了海岸。

examples.en: The succession to the throne was peaceful.
examples.cn: 王位继承过程很和平。

examples.en: She won three races in succession.
examples.cn: 她接连赢了三场比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: succession 是「一连串、继承」；a succession of 是一连串的，in succession 是接连地，succession to the throne 是王位继承，successor 是继任者。

root: 来自拉丁语 successio，由 sub（在后）与 cedere（走）构成，字面是「跟在后面走」，既指位置接替，也指事件一个接一个。

sensesIntro.en: Succession can be a series of things, an inheritance of office, or events in a row.
sensesIntro.cn: succession 可以指一连串事物、职位继承，或接连发生的事件。

core.en: Things following one another in order.
core.cn: 事物按顺序一个跟着一个。

branches.en: A succession of storms hit the coast.
branches.cn: 一连串的暴风雨袭击了海岸。

branches.en: The succession to the throne was peaceful.
branches.cn: 王位继承过程很和平。

branches.en: She won three races in succession.
branches.cn: 她接连赢了三场比赛。

branches.en: A series and a run of wins are both lines of events.
branches.cn: 一串事件和连续获胜，都是事件排成的线。

branches.en: A successor follows the old holder of the seat.
branches.cn: 继任者跟着旧任者坐上位置。

intro.en: Succession builds successive, successor, and successional.
intro.cn: succession 可构成 successive、successor 和 successional。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base cess- meant to go or come after.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cess- 意为走或随后而来。

items.exampleCN: 这个国家经历过许多次继任。

items.example: The prince succeeded to the throne.

items.exampleCN: 这次变动进行得很顺利。

latinEntries.example: Successio is the source of succession.
latinEntries.exampleCN: successio 是 succession 的来源。
succedere 演变为英语的 succeed。

definition_en: to judge the quality, value or importance of something
core_image: 把一件东西放上天平，仔细衡量它的分量
scene: 面试结束后，评委开始评估每位候选人的表现。 After the interviews, the judges began to evaluate each candidate's performance.
sceneCN: 这里 evaluate 是「评估」（第 1 个义项：判断质量、价值或重要性）；句意：面试结束后，评委开始评估每位候选人的表现。

senses.title: Judge quality or value
senses.definition: to judge how good, useful or important something is
senses.definitionCN: 判断某事物有多好、多有用或多重要
senses.example: Teachers evaluate students' progress each term.
senses.exampleCN: 老师每学期评估学生的进步。
senses.why: The word contains value, so evaluating is putting a value on something.
senses.whyCN: 这个词包含 value，因此 evaluate 就是给事物定出价值。

senses.title: Work out an amount
senses.definition: to calculate the amount or effect of something
senses.definitionCN: 计算某事物的数量或影响
senses.example: Engineers evaluated the cost of the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师估算了维修成本。
senses.why: Judging value and calculating cost both weigh something against a standard.
senses.whyCN: 判断价值与计算成本，都是把事物放在标准上衡量。

intro.en: Evaluate comes from French évaluer, to find the value of, from value.
intro.cn: evaluate 源自法语 évaluer（确定价值），来自 value。

items.en: Valere means to be worth or be strong.
items.cn: valere 意为有价值或强健。

items.en: Value means worth.
items.cn: value 意为价值。

items.en: Évaluer means to work out the value.
items.cn: évaluer 意为算出价值。

items.en: Evaluate enters English with the same sense.
items.cn: evaluate 以相同含义进入英语。

items.en: It covers performance, risk and cost.
items.cn: 它涵盖表现、风险与成本。

note.en: Evaluate is close to assess and judge, with value at its core.
note.cn: evaluate 与评估、判断相近，核心是价值。

entries.definition: the act of judging
judging value
worth
to judge the quality of something
to form an opinion about something
to give a value to something

normalIntro.en: Evaluate puts a value on something, like a price tag on a skill.
normalIntro.cn: evaluate 就是给事物标上价值，像给技能贴上价签。

normal.en: Evaluate performance means judge how well someone did.
normal.cn: evaluate performance 意为判断某人做得如何。

normal.en: Evaluate the risk means work out how dangerous it is.
normal.cn: evaluate the risk 意为算出风险有多大。

normal.en: Carefully evaluate means do not decide too quickly.
normal.cn: carefully evaluate 意为不要过快下结论。

normal.en: The noun evaluation names the judging process.
normal.cn: 名词 evaluation 指评估过程。

normal.en: Compare assess: assess is broader, evaluate stresses value.
normal.cn: 对比 assess：assess 更宽泛，evaluate 强调价值。

abstract.en: Picture an object placed on a balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一件物品被放上天平。

abstract.en: Imagine a scorecard filled in row by row.
abstract.cn: 想象一张评分表被一行行填满。

abstract.en: Think of a jeweler holding a stone up to the light.
abstract.cn: 想象珠宝商把宝石举到光下细看。

examples.en: The committee will evaluate all the proposals.
examples.cn: 委员会将评估所有提案。

examples.en: We need to evaluate the risks before we start.
examples.cn: 开始之前我们需要评估风险。

examples.en: It is hard to evaluate a book by its cover.
examples.cn: 仅凭封面很难评价一本书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ value（价值）＋ ate」——把价值算出来，就是评估；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）→ 法语 value（价值）→ évaluer（估价）→ evaluate，核心义「衡量并定出价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Evaluate first judges quality or worth, and then works out an amount or effect.
sensesIntro.cn: evaluate 先判断质量或价值，再计算数量或影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object weighed on a balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：放在天平上称量的物品。

branches.en: Judging quality is the main sense.
branches.cn: 判断质量是主要义项。

branches.en: Calculating an amount is evaluation with numbers.
branches.cn: 计算数量是用数字进行评估。

branches.en: Both quality and cost are weighed against a standard.
branches.cn: 质量与成本都要对照标准衡量。

branches.en: Teachers evaluate, committees evaluate, readers evaluate.
branches.cn: 老师、委员会与读者都会评估。

branches.en: Risk and cost are common evaluated quantities.
branches.cn: 风险与成本是常见的被估量。

intro.en: Evaluate is built on value, with the verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: evaluate 建立在 value 之上，带动词词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, to be worth, gives value and evaluate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）衍生出 value 与 evaluate。

items.example: French évaluer is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 法语 évaluer 是直接来源。
evaluative 描述评价性的评论。

definition_zh: 手腕；腕关节；（衣袖的）腕部
definition_en: the joint or narrow part of the body between the hand and the forearm
core_image: 伸手接过一杯热水时，袖子下面露出的那圈细窄关节
scene: 冬天出门前，老人把围巾拉紧，又把袖口重新拢好。 She twisted her wrist trying to open the stiff jar.
sceneCN: 这里 wrist 是「手腕」（第 1 个义项：手与前臂之间那个关节和细窄部位）；句意为她想拧开那个拧不动的罐子，结果扭伤了手腕。接热水时袖子下露出的那圈细窄关节，就是这个词的印象。

collocations.phrase: wear a watch on your wrist

derivatives.zh: 由 wrist 加 band 复合构成，义为「腕带；腕套」
由 wrist 加指小后缀 -let 构成，义为「腕饰；腕带」
由 wrist 加 -y 构成，义为「用腕力的」

senses.title: The narrow joint
senses.definition: the joint between the hand and the forearm, and the narrow part of the arm just above the hand
senses.definitionCN: 手与前臂之间的关节，也指手部上方那段细窄的手臂
senses.example: She twisted her wrist trying to open the stiff jar.
senses.exampleCN: 她想拧开那个拧不动的罐子，结果扭伤了手腕。
senses.why: The word has named this joint since Old English, so the body part is the earliest and strongest meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古英语起就指这个关节，所以身体部位是最早也最牢固的意思。

senses.title: The edge of a sleeve
senses.definition: the part of a sleeve that covers or ends at the wrist
senses.definitionCN: 袖子覆盖腕部或到腕部为止的那一段
senses.example: He wiped his mouth on his wrist, forgetting there were paper towels.
senses.exampleCN: 他在手腕上擦了擦嘴，忘了有纸巾。
senses.why: Because clothing ends where the joint is, the name of the joint passed to the garment edge that reaches it.
senses.whyCN: 因为衣物正好止于这个关节，关节的名称就传给了伸到那里的那截袖边。

senses.title: The hand at work
senses.definition: the power and movement of the hand controlled from this joint, especially in sport
senses.definitionCN: 由这个关节控制的手部动作与力量，尤指运动中的腕力
senses.example: A good tennis player puts the whole wrist into the serve.
senses.exampleCN: 优秀的网球选手发球时用上整个手腕的力量。
senses.why: Once the joint is the hinge of the hand, the motion it makes can stand for skill itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个关节成了手的铰链，由它做出的动作就可以代表技巧本身。

senses.title: The gentle punishment
senses.definition: a small punishment or gentle warning, in the fixed phrase a slap on the wrist
senses.definitionCN: 轻微的惩罚或温和的警告，用于固定说法 a slap on the wrist
senses.example: The company got a slap on the wrist for the missing labels.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因标签缺失只受到轻微处罚。
senses.why: A slap on the wrist hurts a little but breaks nothing, so the phrase grew into a picture of lenient blame.
senses.whyCN: 打在手腕上有点疼却伤不了人，于是这个说法成了宽容责备的画面。

intro.en: Wrist is a native Germanic word built on a root that suggests twisting, a fitting name for the joint that turns the hand.
intro.cn: wrist 是本土的日耳曼词，词根有「扭转」的意思，用来称那个能转动手的关节十分贴切。

items.en: wrist named the joint of the hand in everyday and medical writing.
items.cn: wrist 在日常与医学文字里都指手上的关节。

items.en: The spelling settled as wrist, keeping the silent w before r.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 wrist，保留了 r 前那个不发音的 w。

items.en: The clothing sense, the part of a sleeve at the joint, appeared in the same period.
items.cn: 衣物义（袖子上到腕部的那一截）也在同一时期出现。

items.en: Compounds such as wristband and wristwatch spread the word into clothing and clocks.
items.cn: wristband、wristwatch 等复合词把它带进衣物与钟表。

items.en: The phrase a slap on the wrist became a standard image of lenient punishment.
items.cn: 说法 a slap on the wrist 成了宽容处罚的标准意象。

note.en: The first group holds words for the same joint area, the second holds neighbouring body parts.
note.cn: 第一组收同一关节部位的词，第二组收相邻的身体部位。

entries.definition: More than one wrist.

The joint in the middle of the arm.
A joint in a finger.

normalIntro.en: Wrist begins with the silent wr that English keeps in writing but drops in speech.
normalIntro.cn: wrist 以不发音的 wr 开头，英语写它、却不读那个 w。

normal.en: The w before r is silent, just as in write and wrong.
normal.cn: r 前的 w 不发音，正如 write 与 wrong。

normal.en: Wrist and write are both spelled with wr but have no shared meaning.
normal.cn: wrist 与 write 都写 wr，但意思毫无关系。

normal.en: Wristband is the band worn at the wrist.
normal.cn: wristband 就是系在腕上的带子。

normal.en: A slap on the wrist means a punishment that barely hurts.
normal.cn: a slap on the wrist 指几乎不疼的处罚。

normal.en: Watch the joint that turns the hand, and you have the wrist.
normal.cn: 盯着那个转动手的关节，那就是 wrist。

abstract.en: A thin ring of bare skin where the sleeve ends.
abstract.cn: 袖口结束时露出的那一圈细窄皮肤。

abstract.en: A wrist turning slowly to check the time.
abstract.cn: 慢慢转动手腕去看时间。

abstract.en: Something small but strong enough to carry a whole body.
abstract.cn: 很小，却结实得能托起整个身体。

examples.en: The nurse held his wrist and counted the beats.
examples.cn: 护士按住他的手腕数脉搏。

examples.en: These gloves are too short and leave the wrist bare.
examples.cn: 这副手套太短，把手腕露在外面。

examples.en: He broke his wrist falling off his bike.
examples.cn: 他从自行车上摔下来，手腕骨折了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞斯特」——表带在手腕上，斯特地提醒你看时间。

root: 古英语 wrist（腕），属日耳曼语族，与德语 Rist（手背、腕）同源，词根一般认为与「扭转」有关；同族词有 wristband、wristlet。

sensesIntro.en: The joint comes first, then the sleeve that reaches it, then the movement it controls, then the gentle punishment measured at the same place.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是关节，再是伸到关节处的袖边，然后是它控制的动作，最后是在同一处量出的轻微处罚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the narrow turning point between hand and arm.
core.cn: 核心意象：手与前臂之间那个细窄的转动点。

branches.en: The body branch: the joint where the hand turns.
branches.cn: 身体分支：手能转动的那处关节。

branches.en: The clothing branch: sleeves end where the joint is.
branches.cn: 衣物分支：袖子止于关节所在的位置。

branches.en: The skill branch: motion from this joint becomes wrist power.
branches.cn: 技巧分支：这里的动作变成腕力。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: a blow that lands here barely hurts.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：打在这里的惩罚几乎不疼。

branches.en: The image branch: a bare ring of skin between glove and sleeve.
branches.cn: 意象分支：手套与袖子之间露出的一圈皮肤。

intro.en: Wrist is a single native stem; English built wristband and wristlet by adding a free word and a small suffix.
intro.cn: wrist 是单一的本土词干；英语加一个独立词和小后缀构成 wristband 与 wristlet。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below belong to a related old medical family.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词属于相关的古老医学词族。

items.meaning: the joint between hand and arm
items.example: The stem carries the whole body meaning.
items.exampleCN: 词干承载了整个身体部位的意思。

items.example: It appears in write, wrong and wrist.

items.meaning: a band worn at the wrist
items.example: The band names what is worn.

items.meaning: a small ornament for the wrist
a watch worn on the wrist
items.example: The watch hangs at the wrist.

items.meaning: a light blow with the open hand
items.example: It explains why the punishment is mild.
items.exampleCN: 它解释了为什么这种处罚是轻的。
这个形容词形容运动中的击球动作。

latinEntries.meaning: to pluck, to bend the wrist

definition_zh: 判断；意见；审判；裁决；判断力
definition_en: an opinion you form about something, or a decision given by a court or an authority
core_image: 天平两端落定，指针停住不再摆动
scene: 会议结束时，大家等着主持人给个说法。 Her judgement on the matter was accepted by everyone at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 judgement 是「判断、意见」（第 1 个义项：对某事形成的看法），句意为她对这件事的判断被在座所有人接受。画面里的物件：会议桌、文件、水杯。

pos.zh: 名词：判断；意见；审判；裁决；判断力

derivatives.zh: 基础词，指法官或评判者
基础动词义，指评判、判断
由 judgement 加 -al 构成，义为「爱评判人的」
加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「判断失误」

senses.title: An opinion formed about something
senses.definition: a considered opinion or conclusion about a situation, person, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 对情形、人或计划经过考虑后形成的看法或结论
senses.example: In my judgement the plan will cost too much.
senses.exampleCN: 依我看，这个计划花费太大。
senses.why: Judging is the act of weighing, and judgement is the scale coming to rest.
senses.whyCN: 评判是称量的动作，judgement 就是秤停下来时的结果。

senses.title: A decision of a court
senses.definition: a formal decision given by a court or judge
senses.definitionCN: 法院或法官作出的正式裁决
senses.example: The court will give its judgement next month.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下个月作出判决。
senses.why: The legal sense fixes the moment when weighing becomes binding.
senses.whyCN: 法律义把「称量」变成「必须执行的时刻」固定下来。

senses.title: The ability to judge well
senses.definition: the ability to make sensible decisions, especially in difficult situations
senses.definitionCN: 作出合理决定的能力，尤指在困难情形中
senses.example: She showed good judgement in a crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 她在危机中表现出很好的判断力。
senses.why: Ability grows out of repeated acts: the noun comes to name the power behind them.
senses.whyCN: 能力来自反复的评判行为，名词于是用来指这些行为背后的力量。

senses.title: A divine or final verdict
senses.definition: a verdict believed to come from a higher power, or a final decision beyond appeal
senses.definitionCN: 被视为来自更高力量的裁决，或无法再上诉的终审
senses.example: The old tale speaks of a day of judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 那个古老的故事讲到审判之日。
senses.why: A verdict thought to be final is the oldest and heaviest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 被看作最终的裁决，是这个词最古老也最沉重的一层。

senses.title: A critical assessment in work
senses.definition: an assessment given by an expert, as in a competition or review
senses.definitionCN: 专家在比赛或评审中给出的评估结论
senses.example: The panel's judgement favoured the second design.
senses.exampleCN: 评审团的评估倾向于第二个设计。
senses.why: Expert weighing is the professional face of the same scale, applied to plans.
senses.whyCN: 专家的称量是同一杆秤的专业面孔，只是用来称方案。

senses.title: The act of forming an opinion
senses.definition: the mental process of comparing and deciding rather than the result
senses.definitionCN: 指比较与决定的思维过程，而不是结果本身
senses.example: Clear criteria make judgement easier.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的准则让评判更容易。
senses.why: Naming the process rather than the result keeps the action side of -ment alive.
senses.whyCN: 指过程而不指结果，让 -ment 里「行为」那一面保留下来。

intro.en: Judgement is judge plus the French-derived noun ending -ment; judge itself comes from Latin judex through French.
intro.cn: judgement 是 judge 加源自法语的 -ment 名词词尾；judge 本身经由法语来自拉丁语 judex。

items.en: judex combined jus, law, and dicere, to say, meaning one who says the law.
items.cn: judex 由 jus「法」和 dicere「说」合成，指宣说法律的人。

items.en: Old French juge named a judge or a court officer.
items.cn: 古法语 juge 指法官或法庭官员。

items.en: English took judge in the thirteenth century and added -ment for the result.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 judge，并加 -ment 表示结果。

items.en: The noun ending -ment came from French and marks an act or its outcome.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ment 来自法语，表示行为或其结果。

items.en: British English kept judgement while American practice prefers judgment.
items.cn: 英式保留 judgement，美式更常用 judgment。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the judge stem; the near-meaning group holds words for decisions and opinions.
note.cn: 形近组共用 judge 词干；近义组收表示裁决与意见的词。

entries.definition: A person who decides, or to form an opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 同源基础词，指法官，也指评判。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same noun.
The court system and its work.
The decision of a jury in a case.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指陪审团的裁决。

entries.definition: A personal view that may not be final.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人看法，不必是定论。

entries.definition: A careful evaluation of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指经过仔细评估得出的结论。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from jus plus dicere, law and say, to a scale that stops moving.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 jus 加 dicere「法与说」走到停下来的那杆秤。

normal.en: Judge joins jus, law, and dicere, to say.
normal.cn: judge 由 jus「法」与 dicere「说」合成。

normal.en: The -ment ending marks the result of an action.
normal.cn: -ment 词尾标记行为的结果。

normal.en: In my judgement is the everyday opinion phrase.
normal.cn: in my judgement 是日常表达意见的说法。

normal.en: A court judgement is written and binding.
normal.cn: court judgement 是书面而具约束力的。

normal.en: British keeps judgement, American prefers judgment.
normal.cn: 英式保留 judgement，美式更常用 judgment。

abstract.en: Judgement is a scale that has stopped swaying.
abstract.cn: 判断是停止摆动的那杆秤。

abstract.en: Half the word is law and half is speech.
abstract.cn: 这个词一半是法律，一半是说话。

abstract.en: Good judgement is a stored supply of quiet decisions.
abstract.cn: 好的判断力是积攒起来的安静决定。

examples.en: In my judgement the delay was avoidable.
examples.cn: 依我看，这次延误本可避免。

examples.en: The court delivered its judgement in a single day.
examples.cn: 法院一天之内就作出了判决。

examples.en: He trusted her judgement more than his own.
examples.cn: 比起自己，他更信任她的判断。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扎之门特」—— 法官一锤扎下去，判定了

root: 拉丁语 jus「法」+ dicere「说」→ judex「宣法者」→ 古法语 juge → 英语 judge → 加 -ment 构成 judgement。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a considered opinion, a court decision, the ability to judge, a final verdict, an expert assessment, and the process itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：经考虑的意见、法院判决、判断力、终审裁决、专家评估，以及评判的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale that sways and finally comes to rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杆摇晃的天平终于停住。

branches.en: THE MEETING ROOM: a view offered and accepted.
branches.cn: 会议室这条线：提出并被接受的一种看法。

branches.en: THE COURT: a written decision with force.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：一份有强制力的书面决定。

branches.en: THE CRISIS: the ability to choose well under pressure.
branches.cn: 危机这条线：压力下做出好选择的能力。

branches.en: THE LAST DAY: a verdict no one can appeal.
branches.cn: 最后一日这条线：无人能再上诉的裁决。

branches.en: THE PANEL: comparing plans and writing the result.
branches.cn: 评审团这条线：比较方案并写下结果。

intro.en: Judgement is judge plus -ment; the Latin pieces underneath are jus and dicere.
intro.cn: judgement 是 judge 加 -ment，底下是 jus 与 dicere 两块拉丁材料。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives come from judex and judicare, from jus and dicere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词来自 judex 与 judicare，由 jus 和 dicere 组成。

definition_en: to prepare land and grow crops, or to help a skill or friendship develop
core_image: 一个人弯着腰在土里松土，旁边是刚冒芽的小苗
scene: 他弯着腰在田里松土，脚边是刚冒芽的小苗。 Farmers cultivate this field twice a year.
sceneCN: 这里 cultivate 指「耕种」（第 1 个义项：翻土并种植作物）；句意是农民每年耕种这块地两次。

senses.title: Work the land
senses.definition: to prepare land and grow crops on it
senses.definitionCN: 翻整土地并在上面种作物
senses.example: They cultivate rice in these fields.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在这些田里种稻。
senses.why: The ground gives back what care is put into it.
senses.whyCN: 土地会回报你放进去的照料。

senses.title: Grow a quality
senses.definition: to help a skill or habit grow over time
senses.definitionCN: 让某种技能或习惯随时间成长
senses.example: Reading cultivates a steady mind.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读培养沉稳的心。
senses.why: A habit is a seed that needs daily water.
senses.whyCN: 习惯是一颗需要每天浇水的种子。

senses.title: Build a relationship
senses.definition: to spend care on a friendship or useful contact
senses.definitionCN: 用心经营友谊或有用的关系
senses.example: He cultivated friends in many cities.
senses.exampleCN: 他在许多城市结交朋友。
senses.why: People, like plants, grow where they are tended.
senses.whyCN: 人和植物一样，在被照料的地方生长。

intro.en: Cultivate comes from Latin cultivare, to till, from colere, to till or to honour.
intro.cn: cultivate 源自拉丁语 cultivare（耕作），更早出自 colere（耕种、敬奉）。

items.en: Colere meant to till the soil and to honour a god.
items.cn: colere 指耕种土地，也指敬奉神灵。

items.en: Cultivare meant to work the land with care.
items.cn: cultivare 指用心整治土地。

items.en: It also described caring for the mind.
items.cn: 它也能形容对心智的照料。

items.en: Cultivate meant to till fields and gardens.
items.cn: cultivate 指耕作田地与园子。

items.en: It extended to manners, skills, and friends.
items.cn: 它扩展到举止、技能与朋友。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cultiv- stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of careful growth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cultiv- 词干，近义组列出其他用心培育的说法。

entries.definition: trained and refined in manner
entries.definitionCN: 举止受过训练而文雅的

entries.definition: of the way a people lives
a small group with strong beliefs
to grow crops on land
to care for something as it grows
to grow stronger or fuller over time
entries.definitionCN: 随时间变得更强或更完整

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand in the soil and end with a friendship kept for years.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从土里的一只手开始，落到维系多年的友谊。

normal.en: Cultivate is care repeated, not a single act.
normal.cn: cultivate 是反复的照料，不是一次性的动作。

normal.en: Turn the soil, drop the seed, wait.
normal.cn: 翻土，下种，然后等。

normal.en: A skill grows like a plant, on small daily water.
normal.cn: 本事像植物，靠每天一点点水长大。

normal.en: You can cultivate beans, a habit, or a friend.
normal.cn: 你可以种豆，也可以培养习惯或结交朋友。

normal.en: Whatever is cultivated stops being wild.
normal.cn: 被栽培过的东西，就不再是野生的。

abstract.en: Picture a hoe turning dark soil in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象清晨一把锄头翻起黑土。

abstract.en: Picture a green shoot beside a careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只谨慎的手旁有一株绿芽。

abstract.en: Picture two people meeting again after years.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人多年后再次相见。

examples.en: They cultivate vegetables behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们在屋后种菜。

examples.en: She cultivated the habit of walking at dawn.
examples.cn: 她养成了天亮散步的习惯。

examples.en: Good leaders cultivate the people around them.
examples.cn: 好的领导者培养身边的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cultivate 记成「照料」：cult 是耕种，反复照料，土地和本事都会长。

root: 源自拉丁语 cultivare（耕作），更早出自 colere（耕种、敬奉）；本义是翻土种地，后引申为培养能力、习惯与人际关系。

sensesIntro.en: From working the soil, to growing a skill, to tending a friendship.
sensesIntro.cn: 从整治土地，到培养本事，再到经营友谊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand loosening soil around a young shoot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在新苗周围松土。

branches.en: Land must be broken and planted before it feeds anyone.
branches.cn: 土地要先翻开放种，才能养活人。

branches.en: A skill is watered in small amounts every day.
branches.cn: 本事靠每天一点点的浇灌。

branches.en: Friendship is a plant that needs regular care.
branches.cn: 友谊是一株需要常常照料的植物。

branches.en: Soil and mind answer the same kind of care.
branches.cn: 土地与心智回应同一种照料。

branches.en: Habits and friendships both die when neglected.
branches.cn: 习惯与友谊一旦荒废都会死去。

intro.en: Cultivate belongs to the Latin colere family, which also gives culture and agriculture.
intro.cn: cultivate 属于拉丁语 colere 一族，culture 与 agriculture 也出自这里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin colere, to till and to honour, is the root under cultivation and culture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 colere（耕种、敬奉）是 cultivation 与 culture 背后的根。

items.meaning: the act of tilling or developing
a person or machine that tills
items.example: The cultivator broke the hard soil.
Uncultivated land lay beyond the fence.

items.meaning: the way a people lives and thinks
items.meaningCN: 一个族群的生存与思维方式
items.exampleCN: 文化塑造我们打招呼的方式。

items.meaning: of a people's way of life
items.example: The city has a rich cultural life.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市文化生活丰富。
